entry.title: Proof that computing normal-form correlated equilibria in extensive-form games is in PPAD
entry.summary: Computing Normal-Form Correlated Equilibria in Extensive-Form Games is in PPAD arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how hard it is to find normal-form correlated equilibria (NFCE) in extensive-form games with perfect recall, a major open problem in algorithmic game theory. The authors show the problem lies in the PPAD class for any number of players. They also prove that computing such an NFCE whose support size is quadratic in the game size is PPAD-hard, even for two-player games. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that computing normal-form correlated equilibria in extensive-form games lies in PPAD, and prove PPAD-hardness for two-player games with quadratic support.

entry.title: DéjàVu: Reaching Majority Agreement by Repeating an Opinion
entry.summary: DéjàVu: Plurality Consensus by First Repetition arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper analyzes DéjàVu, a simple protocol in which each agent samples one random agent per round and adopts the first opinion it sees twice, then resets its memory. The rule needs no frequency counters or knowledge of population size or number of opinions. The authors prove that, when the initial plurality has a sufficient lead, the protocol reaches consensus on that opinion quickly with high probability, and is asymptotically never slower than h-majority protocols under the same conditions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a counter-free plurality consensus protocol using first repetition, proving convergence bounds and comparing them to h-majority dynamics.

entry.title: Computing fair allocations of goods under budget-style size limits
entry.summary: Computing Feasible EF1 Allocations under Generalized Assignment Constraints arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies fairly dividing indivisible goods when each agent's bundle must fit within her budget and goods can have different sizes for different agents, with unallocated goods going to charity. It shows that feasible envy-freeness up to one good (FEF1) allocations can be computed in strongly polynomial time, provided each agent's value can be almost exactly maximized over her feasible bundles. The allocation can also be made approximately envy-free up to any good while keeping nearly half the Nash welfare of a given allocation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend FEF1 computability to agent-specific sizes, giving a strongly polynomial algorithm, a near-tight quadratic repair bound, and NP-hardness results.

entry.title: Optimal (1,1)-criss-cross deletion-correcting codes with linear-time encoding and decoding
entry.summary: Optimal texorpdfstring(1,1)(1,1)-Criss-Cross Deletion-Correcting Codes with Linear-Time Encoder and Decoder arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies q-ary n×n arrays subject to a (1,1)-criss-cross deletion, which removes one row and one column. It first derives a sphere-packing type lower bound on the redundancy of codes correcting such deletions. It then gives two constructions: the first has redundancy 2n-1+2log_q n+o_q(1), matching the bound up to a vanishing term, with O_q(n^2) decoding; the second has redundancy 2n+2log_q n+O_q(1), with O_q(n^2) encoding and decoding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a sphere-packing lower bound on redundancy for (1,1)-criss-cross deletion codes and construct near-tight codes with linear-time encoding and decoding.

entry.title: Proof of the functional batch conjecture and its extension to all finite fields
entry.summary: The Functional Batch Conjecture And Its Extension To All Finite Fields arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies a coding scheme in which servers store all nonzero linear combinations of s information symbols over a finite field. The authors prove that this code is a functional batch code for every finite field and every s≥1, with list size (q^s+q-2)/2, and that this list size cannot be increased. They also determine the minimum length of such functional batch codes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the functional batch conjecture to all finite fields, reporting tight list sizes and minimum code lengths with proofs.

entry.title: Learning equilibria in congestion games from resource load and cost feedback
entry.summary: Last-Iterate Equilibrium Learning in Symmetric Congestion Games under Semi-Bandit Feedback arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how players in symmetric congestion games with atomic players can learn mixed Nash equilibria, observing both costs and loads of chosen resources. The authors add a quadratic consensus penalty that makes the potential function globally strongly convex, with the symmetric equilibrium as its unique minimizer. They propose a variant of online projected gradient descent and show convergence rates in expectation, with the played profile converging to equilibrium almost surely.

entry.title: A study of distance properties of Huffman sequences
entry.summary: On the Distance Properties of Huffman Sequences arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies pairwise distances between sequences that share the same aperiodic autocorrelation function. The authors show that these distances are determined by a ternary signed pattern that encodes relative zero flips between spectral factors. For Huffman sequences, they prove that dihedral symmetries of the zeros preserve pairwise distances and derive lower bounds on the minimum distance. The results provide a starting point for designing codes with fixed autocorrelation, which are relevant to integrated sensing and communication.

entry.title: PipeAxes: Separating Compute and Communication Granularity in Pipeline-Parallel LLM Serving
entry.summary: PipeAxes: Decoupling Compute and Communication Granularities for Pipeline-Parallel LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 26, 2026PipeAxes is a serving system for large language models run with pipeline parallelism across GPUs. It splits wide prefill batches into slices of a few layers so decoding can run between them, and compresses activations with a fused Triton Hadamard-INT4 codec sent in independently sized row groups over parallel TCP sockets. A scheduler uses latency slack to choose batch width, slice depth, and row-group size. The paper reports results from 97 replays covering 5,016 requests, including throughput and latency comparisons with baselines and accuracy changes for INT4 transport relative to BF16.

entry.title: High-performance epidemic models: comparing mobility methods and their speed on CPUs and GPUs
entry.summary: High-performance metapopulation models for epidemic emergencies: Scalability and performance of implicit and explicit mobility representations on CPUs and GPUs arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper compares two ways of modeling population movement in spatial epidemic models: implicit coupling through transition and transmission intensities, and explicit tracking of traveling subpopulations by home and current location. A four-patch experiment shows the two trajectories stay close, but diverge as the mobility cycle length increases. The authors present CPU and GPU parallel implementations and test networks of up to 16,384 patches on 128 CPU cores and NVIDIA A100 and H100 GPUs. In a synthesized central European outbreak, a worldwide pandemic with 12,865 patches and four billion state variables runs in 24 seconds on GPUs.

entry.title: Same seed, different top prediction: whether AlphaFold 3 gives the same top structure across chips
entry.summary: Same Seed, Different Top Prediction: Cross-Platform Reproducibility of AlphaFold 3 Inference on TPUs, GPUs, and CPUs arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines whether AlphaFold 3 returns the same top-ranked structure when the same input, weights, seed, and settings run on different hardware. Tests on two TPU generations, three NVIDIA GPUs, and an Intel CPU across 60 protein-ligand complexes found the top sample changed in 18.0% of predictions when switching TPU generations. Structures changed only slightly, with correct-versus-incorrect pose switches in about 3.3% to 3.7% of predictions. The authors recommend reporting the device and all near-tied samples.

entry.title: Functional Factor Graphs and Functional Sum-Product Algorithm for Estimating Unknown Functions
entry.summary: Functional Factor Graphs and the Functional Sum-Product Algorithm arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper extends factor graphs and the sum-product algorithm to unknowns that are functions, such as waveforms, time-varying channels, and continuous-aperture array currents. Because functions lack probability density functions, densities are measured relative to each function's prior, so messages become likelihood ratios. For Gaussian models, the functional sum-product algorithm reduces to Gaussian belief propagation with kernels, and its convergence condition does not depend on the grid. Multi-user detection simulations show that scalar belief propagation on grid samples slows under refinement, and that sampling first can fail even for smooth priors.

entry.title: Weak Negotiation Function: A New Tool for Weak Subgame-Perfect Equilibria in Graph Games
entry.summary: The Weak Negotiation Function arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies subgame-perfect equilibria (SPEs), a refinement of Nash equilibria that rules out non-credible threats, in graph games. It introduces the weak negotiation function, a variant of the existing negotiation function, and shows that weak SPEs can be characterised by it in the same way SPEs are. Using this characterisation, the authors show that deciding whether a mean-payoff game has a weak SPE with payoffs in a given interval is NP-complete, and give a new proof that the same problem for Büchi games is in P. They also present a much shorter proof of weak SPE existence in mean-payoff games.

entry.title: Four classes of few-weight linear codes built from simplicial complexes
entry.summary: Four Classes of Few-Weight Linear Codes over u𝔽_q+u²𝔽_q+u³𝔽_q from Simplicial Complexes arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper constructs linear codes over the commutative non-unital ring uF_q+u²F_q+u³F_q with u⁴=0, using simplicial complexes in F_q^m and their complements. For codes defined by two nonempty simplicial complexes, the lengths and F_q-dimensions are determined. Using an F_q-linear Gray map and exponential sums, the parameters and Lee weight distributions of four code classes are found, with two, at most five, at most four, and at most eight nonzero Lee weights. Puncturing the Gray images gives projective codes with dual minimum distance three.

entry.title: Several classes of few-weight linear codes built from Weil sums
entry.summary: Several classes of few-weight linear codes based on Weil sums arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper constructs several classes of p-ary linear codes, where p is an odd prime, using Weil sums and a defining-set construction based on bivariate forms. Using quadratic form theory and Weil sums over finite fields, the parameters and weight distributions of these codes are fully determined. The construction yields several families of three-weight or four-weight linear codes, and most of them are shown to be minimal.

entry.title: A local-counting method for detecting induced paths in distributed networks
entry.summary: A Local-Counting Approach for Distributed Induced Path Detection arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how to detect induced paths in distributed networks with limited bandwidth. The authors propose a local-counting approach that counts signals over random colorings to tell induced paths apart from cycles. Using this approach, they give distributed algorithms for detecting induced P4, P5, and P6 with improved round complexities.

entry.title: Semantic graph decoding for text-carrying LDPC codes
entry.summary: Semantic Tanner-Graph Decoding for LDPC Codes arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a semantic Tanner graph for transmitting text with LDPC codes and develops semantic-factor-aided belief propagation (SF-BP) decoding. Each text token gets a semantic factor, which a fine-tuned language model uses to assign a posterior distribution over possible tokens. Simulations for the (1248, 1040) LDPC code at 4 dB show SF-BP substantially lowers block error rate and raises Sentence-BERT similarity compared with conventional BP.

entry.title: CoordRoute: coordinated routing of requests across several language models to maximize total value within a fixed compute budget
entry.summary: CoordRoute: Coordinated Multi-Model Routing for Maximum Compute-Budget Utility arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how to send requests to one of several large language models of different sizes when the requests share a fixed compute budget. The authors propose coordinated routing that predicts each model's output and cost, plans choices against later requests, and corrects routing during generation to maximize total satisfaction. On Azure Conversation and BurstGPT traces, the method improves total satisfaction by 18.72% over the strongest existing router.

entry.title: Asymmetric Speculative Decoding: Speeding Up Language Model Drafts by Giving the Draft Model Examples
entry.summary: Asymmetric Speculative Decoding: Unlocking In-Context Learning in Draft Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines why speculative decoding, a method that speeds up large language model inference by drafting and verifying tokens in parallel, gives smaller gains on reasoning tasks. It identifies that giving both models the same prompt makes the draft model's guesses often rejected. The authors propose Asymmetric Speculative Decoding (AsymSpec), a training-free method that supplies the draft model with task-relevant example solutions, and report 2.29 to 4.95 times speedups over autoregressive decoding across reasoning, code generation, and summarization tasks.

entry.title: Certified Outage Bounds for RIS-Assisted NOMA with Thermal Energy Harvesting
entry.summary: Certified Outage Bounds for RIS-Assisted NOMA with Source-Side Thermal Energy Harvesting arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) with source-side thermal energy harvesting. It extends the model to include Poisson interference and derives two-sided outage bounds. The authors show that Gaussian approximations can cause opposite power-sizing errors and, under another power convention, false feasibility with Gamma-distributed interference. Propagated Chernoff bounds are used to give sufficient designs, with results limited to the specified model and tested regimes.

entry.title: Extracting work from any single binary-like sequence using finite-state engines
entry.summary: Universal Work Extraction from Individual Sequences by Finite--State Information Engines arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies information engines that interact with a heat bath, a work reservoir, and a tape carrying a deterministic sequence over a finite alphabet. The engines are cascades of autonomous ratchets with fixed energy levels and detailed-balance dynamics. The authors prove a converse bound on extractable work in terms of the empirical block entropies of the sequence, and show it can be achieved universally by engines whose energy levels do not depend on the sequence.

entry.title: Going beyond welfarism: a more affordable proportional approval voting rule
entry.summary: Beyond the Limits of Welfarism: An Affordable Proportional Approval Voting Rule arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies multiwinner elections with approval ballots, extending Proportional Approval Voting (PAV) by allowing committees of varying size while penalizing larger ones. It proposes an exact rule and a polynomial-time local-search variant, both yielding outcomes that admit a priceable completion and, on laminar instances, a laminar-proportional one. The analysis uses two marginal stability conditions to derive welfare and coverage guarantees and improves the best known lower bound on the utilitarian ratio of standard PAV. ★★★★ Notable: The authors go beyond welfarism with variable-size committees and penalties, obtaining priceable and laminar-proportional guarantees and improving PAV's utilitarian ratio lower bound.

entry.title: Stability of Lattice Quantizers for Compressed Data Under Small Changes
entry.summary: Quantization and Codebook Stability of Euclidean and KL Lattice Quantizers arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies whether compressed representations and Huffman codebooks stay the same when raw data undergoes small edits. It analyzes two lattice-based quantizers on the probability simplex, the Euclidean Lattice Quantizer (ELQ) and the KL Quantizer (KLQ), deriving bounds on quantization stability and KL distortion. Simulations compare these quantizers with an existing compander-based quantizer, showing trade-offs between KL distortion, codebook stability, and encoded length under random deletions.

entry.title: Exact minimum distances of primitive narrow-sense BCH codes
entry.summary: Exact Minimum Distances of Primitive Narrow-Sense BCH Codes: At and Beyond the Bose Distance arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper determines the exact minimum distances of two families of primitive narrow-sense BCH codes of length q^m-1, where q is a prime power and m≥4. For the first family, the minimum distance and Bose distance both equal the designed distance. For the second family, the Bose distance equals the designed distance while the minimum distance is smaller by q^s. The authors construct zero-sets from quadratic forms, use divisibility of weights in punctured generalized Reed-Muller codes for lower bounds, and derive explicit dimension formulas by counting cyclotomic cosets.

entry.title: Research on non-manipulability and approachability in games with more than two players
entry.summary: Non-manipulability and Approachability Beyond Two-Player Games arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies how n-1 independent learners in a repeated n-player general game can avoid being exploited by a strategic optimizer while keeping low regret. It introduces a set of algorithms that each achieve sublinear swap regret and that jointly guarantee non-manipulability. The authors show that these algorithms require computing a Nash equilibrium at every step, a cost they argue is inherent in general games.

entry.title: Vector quantized information bottleneck defenses against adversarial attacks on modulation classifiers
entry.summary: Vector Quantized Information Bottleneck Mitigation of Adversarial Attacks on Modulation Classifiers arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies machine-learning-based automatic modulation classification for radio-frequency signals, which is vulnerable to adversarial attacks. The authors compare two frameworks that use discrete information bottlenecks: a vector quantized variational autoencoder (VQVAE) that reconstructs inputs to suppress perturbations, and a vector quantized classifier (VQC) built into the classifier itself. Under white-box attacks, discrete bottlenecks significantly improve robustness, with VQVAE outperforming its continuous VAE counterpart and VQC achieving strong robustness without signal reconstruction.

entry.title: Simulation-Assisted Radio Map Reconstruction Using Sparse Field Measurements
entry.summary: Simulation-Assisted Radio Map Reconstruction with Sparse Field Measurements arXiv · Nov 18, 2026This paper proposes SA-PBDW, a method that combines propagation simulations with sparse field measurements for radio map reconstruction. It jointly estimates background coefficients and a spatial correction to account for differences between simulated and measured power distributions. Dense measurements were collected at an urban site for multiple transmitter positions, and the method was evaluated on this data and RadioMapSeer. It reportedly achieves better accuracy and structural fidelity than benchmark methods at reduced sampling rates.

entry.title: Relative Entropy Bounds Under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints
entry.summary: Relative Entropy under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints: Sharp Bounds and Extremizers arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper derives a sharp upper bound on the relative entropy D(P‖Q) in terms of the two ordered chi-squared divergences χ²(P‖Q) and χ²(Q‖P). Two pairs of Bernoulli distributions attain both bounds simultaneously. Consequently, if one chi-squared divergence tends to zero while the other stays uniformly bounded, both relative entropies tend to zero. Under exact constraints, the infimum of D(P‖Q) is zero and is not attained on alphabets with at least three elements.

entry.title: Improved Bounds for Downward-Closed Delegation
entry.summary: Improved Downward-Closed Delegation Bounds arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies delegated choice under a downward-closed feasibility constraint, where principal and agent values may be correlated across items but items are independent. The authors give a deterministic, agent-oblivious menu that guarantees the principal more than 29/70 (about 0.41429) of the expected offline optimum under every best response, including ties resolved against the principal. The previous best guarantee for this setting was 0.1098. ★★★★ Notable: For downward-closed delegation, the authors give a deterministic menu guaranteeing the principal over 29/70 of the expected offline optimum, improving the prior 0.1098, and report several upper bounds

entry.title: Envy-free cake division among five people
entry.summary: Envy-Free Cake-Cutting for Five Agents arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies envy-free cake-cutting, where a divisible resource is split among agents with different preferences so that no agent prefers another's piece. The authors develop a simpler approach that gives an efficient algorithm for five agents, producing a connected ε-envy-free division using O(log^3(1/ε)) queries. They also provide a new existence proof for the five-agent case that relies only on the intermediate value theorem. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a simpler approach giving a polylogarithmic-query connected envy-free algorithm for five agents, with an existence proof using only the intermediate value theorem.

entry.title: Breaking the Square-Root Barrier for Linear Swap Regret in Polyhedral Games
entry.summary: Breaking the Square-Root Barrier for Linear Swap Regret in Polyhedral Games arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies linear swap regret in self-play games, measuring cumulative regret against all affine self-maps of each player's strategy polytope. For compact polytopes defined by linear inequalities, the authors present a deterministic uncoupled dynamic with regret scaling as a polynomial in the game's description length times T to the 1/3 power, independent of the number of vertices. For perfect-recall n-player extensive-form games, they achieve logarithmic regret against all linear deviations, extending prior logarithmic trigger-regret results. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report breaking the square-root barrier for linear swap regret, achieving T^{1/3} on polytopes and logarithmic regret in extensive-form games.

entry.title: (1-ε)-MMS Allocations: Near-Fair Division of Indivisible Items
entry.summary: (1-ǎrepsilon)-MMS Allocations arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies maximin share (MMS) allocations, a fairness criterion, of m indivisible items among n agents with additive valuations. The authors prove that for both goods and chores, the optimal MMS approximation factor converges to 1 as n grows. For fixed ε and sufficiently large n, they give polynomial-time algorithms computing a (1-ε)-MMS allocation for goods and a (1+ε)-MMS allocation for chores. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show the optimal MMS approximation factor tends to 1 as agents grow, with polynomial-time algorithms for goods and chores.

entry.title: Approximate maximin share (MMS) fair allocation with many agents
entry.summary: Approximate MMS allocations for large number of agents arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies allocating indivisible items to agents with non-negative additive valuations, using the maximin share (MMS) fairness benchmark. It proves that for every ρ<1 there is an n_ρ such that any instance with at least n_ρ agents admits a ρ-MMS allocation. This result was previously posed as a conjecture by the authors and had been shown only when the number of items is at most (2−ε)n. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that for enough agents a rho-MMS allocation always exists, resolving a conjecture, using new block-matching techniques.

entry.title: Sequence design for flat-top beams: controlling passband ripple and stopband leakage together
entry.summary: Sequences for Flat-Top Beams arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies sequences for flat-top beams, which are used in radar and communication systems. Using Fourier analysis, the authors examine the asymptotic behavior of passband ripple and stopband leakage. They show that finite-alphabet sequences, including binary and quaternary ones, cannot make both quantities vanish simultaneously as length grows. For infinite-alphabet sequences, generalized step-chirp (GSC) sequences satisfy both requirements under specified conditions on length-bandwidth product and step size. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend sequence design beyond full-band flatness to flat-top beams, contrasting finite and infinite alphabets and giving GSC convergence rates.

entry.title: Self-orthogonal minimal codes built from n-to-1 mappings
entry.summary: Self-Orthogonal Minimal Codes from n-to-1 Mappings arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies linear codes derived from n-to-1 mappings over finite fields that are both self-orthogonal and minimal. Such codes can simultaneously yield quantum error-correcting codes and secret-sharing schemes. The authors use right greatest common divisors of skew polynomials to determine the kernel dimensions of associated linearized polynomials, which gives the codes' weight distributions. They treat two newly constructed families and one known family, proving that all resulting codes are minimal and self-orthogonal. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use right gcds of skew polynomials to find kernel dimensions, deriving weight distributions and proving minimal, self-orthogonal codes for three n-to-1 families.

entry.title: Generalized tensor parallelism for training trillion-parameter LLMs at over 10 EFLOP/s
entry.summary: Generalized Tensor Parallelism: Powering Trillion-Parameter LLM Training at 10+ EFLOP/s arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes generalized tensor parallelism (GTP), a framework that unifies data, tensor, sequence, context parallelism and fully sharded data parallelism as special cases for linear layers. It schedules parameter all-gathers per matrix multiplication rather than per Transformer block to balance communication hiding and memory use. The authors report 13.0 model EFLOP/s and 98% weak-scaling efficiency for an internal 2-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model on 12,288 GB300 GPUs. Throughput is reported as 1.05 to 1.55 times that of Megatron-FSDP and 1.27 to 1.31 times that of a tuned 3D-parallel recipe on 256 to 1,024 GPUs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify five parallelisms into generalized tensor parallelism, scheduling all-gathers per GEMM; the abstract reports throughput gains on a 2T MoE and 256–1,024 GPUs.

entry.title: Trade-offs between queries and samples for revenue maximization
entry.summary: Query-Sample Tradeoffs for Revenue Maximization arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies revenue maximization against a single buyer whose value follows an unknown distribution. The learner can combine value samples, which reveal the buyer's full value, with pricing queries, which only reveal whether a fresh buyer accepts a chosen price. The authors give tight or almost tight bounds on how many extra pricing queries are needed as the sample budget shrinks, for monotone-hazard-rate, regular, quasi-monotone-hazard-rate, and quasi-regular distributions. For quasi-MHR distributions, additional samples reduce the query requirement by polynomial factors, while for MHR and regular distributions, a small fraction of samples still leaves the query cost close to the single-sample level. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize the full sample-query tradeoff for revenue maximization, giving tight bounds for MHR and regular families and removing a logarithmic factor.

entry.title: Coverage of Terahertz Networks with Blockages and Scattering
entry.summary: Coverage of THz Networks in Presence of Blockages and Scattering arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper develops an analytical framework for cellular terahertz networks that accounts for blockages, scattering elements, directionality, atmospheric absorption, and noise. Scattering elements are modeled as a Poisson point process, and the Laplace transform of their aggregate interference is derived, alongside coverage probability, SINR, rate coverage, and area spectral efficiency. The results are validated by Monte Carlo simulation that preserves the correlation of incident power across scatterers. The authors identify a critical scatterer density above which coverage falls steeply, so scattering interference must be included in heavily cluttered deployments.

entry.title: Adding a write operation to history-independent LL/SC objects
entry.summary: Making History-Independence-Preserving LL/SC Writable arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper considers a randomized implementation of LL/SC objects for multiple processes that preserves quiescent history independence but does not support an unconditional write operation. The authors show how to add a randomized wait-free write operation. They state that this addition leaves the asymptotic step and space complexity of the implementation unchanged.

entry.title: Fast Algorithms for Computing the V-BLAST Column Permutation
entry.summary: High-Performance Algorithms for Computing the V-BLAST Permutation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes two efficient algorithms for computing the V-BLAST column permutation, or an approximation of it, used in QR factorization within integer least-squares solvers for receivers in multi-symbol communication systems. The first algorithm uses Householder reflections, is numerically stable, and has a short critical path, but does not exploit cache memory efficiently. The second is a randomized algorithm that approximates the V-BLAST permutation, has a short critical path, and effectively uses cache memory. The authors prove approximation properties of the randomized method and show experimentally that both algorithms outperform existing ones, both in isolation and within an integer least-squares solver.

entry.title: Estimating GPU Roofline arithmetic intensity using off-the-shelf LLMs and compiler artifacts
entry.summary: Estimating GPU Roofline Arithmetic Intensity with Off-the-Shelf LLMs and Compiler Artifacts arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines whether general-purpose large language models can estimate GPU Roofline arithmetic intensity, the ratio of floating-point operations to device-memory bytes, without running the target workload. The authors test three models across 179 combinations of kernels, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, parallel runtimes, and code variants, comparing source-only queries, queries with compiler artifacts, and sandboxed agentic analysis. Adding compiler artifacts raises the share of estimates within 1.20 times the profiled values, and bandwidth-bound or compute-bound classifications are correct in 78-92% of runs. The authors suggest such estimates could help prioritize optimization when GPU access is limited, and identify cache-dependent device-memory traffic as the main obstacle to precise prediction.

entry.title: Scalable placement planning for split LLM serving across mixed edge devices
entry.summary: Scalable Placement for Disaggregated LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Fleets arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents Spade, a placement planner for disaggregated large language model serving with pipeline replication across heterogeneous edge clusters. It uses dominance-based pruning to shrink the search space, combined with water-filling layer partitioning and a bounded multidimensional knapsack formulation under a congestion-aware objective. On a synthetic 30-device fleet, Spade finds the optimal placement in 441 ms, while a genetic-search baseline takes about two hours and yields a 19.7% worse congestion objective.

entry.title: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes
entry.summary: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how much the left-to-right species order of interacting particles on the integer lattice reveals about their initial configuration. Under long-range swaps of distinct species, deleting the stronger particles yields coordinates with independent Poisson increments. For finitely supported initial laws, the mutual information between a function of the initial configuration and the species order decays like 1/t, with the long-time coefficient determined by Gaussian order statistics and conditional means.

entry.title: Combining physical layer security and symmetric encryption to protect rate-splitting multiple access
entry.summary: Combining Physical Layer Security and Symmetric Encryption to Secure Rate-Splitting Multiple Access arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a hybrid physical layer security scheme for rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) in downlink MU-MIMO systems. All user data is symmetrically encrypted, and the key information is embedded within the private messages secured by physical layer security. The precoder design is formulated as a non-convex spectral efficiency maximization problem and solved using successive convex approximation.

entry.title: Energy as a Service-Level Objective: attributing energy use to individual transactions
entry.summary: Energy as a Service-Level Objective: Transaction-Level Energy Attribution arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This thesis examines how energy objectives can become practical engineering tools rather than reporting metrics, using Site Reliability Engineering as a guiding model. It proposes attributing shared and auxiliary energy consumption to successful transactions. Planned experiments compare aggregate, request-normalized and useful-work-based indicators under controlled observability changes and injected failures.

entry.title: Confidence bounds on watermark signal share in LLM text
entry.summary: Simultaneous Inference for Watermark Proportions in LLM-Generated Text arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how to measure the share of watermark signals that remain in text generated by large language models, both for whole documents and for passages chosen during review. The authors propose structure-adaptive closed testing (SACT), which yields simultaneous lower confidence bounds on watermark proportions. Under a conditional null model, the bounds remain valid at finite sample sizes even if the working model is misspecified. Simulations across two watermarking mechanisms and varying signal strengths and densities show SACT generally has higher power than competing methods.

entry.title: Parallel Memory Management in Goose, C++, and Rust: Allocation, Reclamation, and Scaling Experiments
entry.summary: Parallel Memory Management in Goose, C++, and Rust: An Experimental Study of Allocation, Reclamation, and Scaling arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper experimentally compares Goose v2026.3, a compiler-managed memory system, with C++ and Rust implementations on parallel benchmarks of dynamic arrays and binary trees. The tree tests include both individually allocated nodes and contiguous arenas, and the study measures execution time, memory usage, and strong and weak scaling on a four-core, eight-thread workstation. The authors find that compiler-managed storage can be effective for parallel workloads with predictable object lifetimes. They also conclude that execution time alone does not capture its memory and scalability trade-offs.

entry.title: Lossless Re-Encoding of Vorbis and Opus Audio Files
entry.summary: Lossless Re-Encoding of Vorbis and Opus Audio Files arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents Balrogg, a lossless recompressor that replaces the entropy coding in Ogg Vorbis and Ogg Opus audio files with adaptive context mixing models. At default settings it shrinks Vorbis music by 16.2%, Vorbis speech by 10.6%, and Opus speech by 5.4%, while general-purpose tools such as xz and zstd save at most 4.1% on the same files. Encoding and decoding are symmetric, run at 1.8 to 3.2 MB/s per core, and use less than 12 MiB of memory.

entry.title: ModelLess: A Serverless System for Sharing GPUs Across Tiers of LLM Inference
entry.summary: ModelLess: A Serverless System for Multi-Tier LLM Inference on Shared GPUs arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper presents ModelLess, a serverless system for large language model inference that scales idle services to zero by putting instances to sleep with weights kept in host memory. Freed GPUs are lent to lower-priority tiers, with billing based on the time a service holds GPUs. Each tier has eviction semantics that define what state may be lost on preemption, and a protocol ensures requests are re-enqueued rather than aborted. Replaying traces from 1,100 H20 cards, the authors estimate an idealized upper bound of about 38% of GPU time could be lent.

entry.title: RePrism: Scheduling LLM Agent Requests and Prompt Representations Together
entry.summary: RePrism: Joint Request and Representation Scheduling for LLM Agent Serving arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents RePrism, a serving system for LLM agent workflows that jointly chooses which ready request to serve and which representation of its prompt to use. The scheduler ranks request-representation pairs by combining immediate value with estimated future value from the visible workflow, while the resource manager allocates GPU memory to LoRA adapters and cached key-value states. On a dynamic workload, RePrism is reported to achieve 1.37 times the request throughput and reduce P95 session completion time by a factor of 4.10 compared with S-LoRA.

entry.title: Reliable AI agent execution on collaborative edge devices using a world model
entry.summary: Reliability-aware AI Agent Execution in Collaborative Edge Computing: A World Model Approach arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how to keep AI agent tasks running reliably across user-controlled edge devices when nodes fail or wireless links are disrupted. It formulates an online problem that jointly chooses resource allocation, state protection, and recovery targets to maximize task success before deadlines. The authors build a world model that simulates future execution and recovery under candidate actions, and use world model-based model predictive control (WorldMPC) with Monte Carlo rollouts to optimize decisions. Experiments in simulation and a real-world testbed show WorldMPC achieves higher task success rates than baselines.

entry.title: Joule is FLOP: a framework for tensor-core kernel optimization under GPU power limits
entry.summary: Joule is FLOP: Optimizing Tensor-Core Kernels Beyond Latency Hiding at the GPU Power Wall arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper presents Joule, a framework showing that when a tensor-core kernel's power stays near the GPU's cap, runtime roughly equals energy per call divided by that cap, so reducing data movement can raise clock speed and shorten execution. Joule combines hardware event counts, data-path energy costs, and voltage scaling to predict sustained frequency and runtime, and defines a power-aware speed of light bound. On B200 the energy model has a 0.69% mean prediction error, and its GEMM achieves geometric-mean speedups over cuBLAS of 4.94%, 6.64%, and 2.12% on B200, H100 NVL, and RTX PRO 6000.

entry.title: Norn: Context-length-aware placement of weights and KV cache for offloaded LLM inference
entry.summary: Norn: Context-Length-Aware Optimization of Weight and KV Cache Placement for Offloaded LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents Norn, a method for running large language models on a single memory-limited GPU by offloading model weights and the KV cache to host memory. Norn precomputes several execution plans and switching points offline, then switches between them during decoding as the context length grows. Experiments on Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B across two single-GPU systems show up to 16.8× lower end-to-end latency than Pipelined Sharding and 4.2× over an oracle variant with known input and output lengths.

entry.title: Insertion-deletion distance of linear codes under random coordinate permutations
entry.summary: The Insertion-Deletion Distance of Linear Codes under Random Coordinate Permutations arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies the maximum insertion-deletion (insdel) distance achievable by permuting the coordinates of a fixed linear code. Using a link between common subsequences of codewords and noncrossing matchings in bipartite graphs, it derives probabilistic lower bounds for random coordinate permutations over large alphabets. It also gives bounds for MDS and full-length Reed-Solomon codes, and explicit constructions of full-length RS codes over square fields achieving order-optimal insdel distance.

entry.title: Parity-check matrices and MDS/NMDS properties of non-GRS linear codes
entry.summary: Parity-check matrices and their MDS or NMDS properties for several classes of non-GRS type linear codes arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies several classes of non-GRS linear codes, including column-twisted generalized Reed-Solomon (TGRS) codes and modified GRS codes. The authors build explicit parity-check matrices using code extensions with Cramer's rule and direct constructions. They also give a necessary and sufficient condition for a subclass of twisted generalized Roth-Lempel codes to be maximum distance separable (MDS). For one-column TGRS codes, the paper proves they are either MDS or near MDS (NMDS).

entry.title: Explicit constructions of MDS cyclic codes from rational function fields
entry.summary: Explicit Constructions of MDS Cyclic Codes from Rational Function Fields arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a unified method for building maximum distance separable (MDS) cyclic codes over finite fields using rational function fields. The construction uses evaluation places forming one orbit under a cyclic automorphism group, recovering known existence results for certain code lengths. For odd divisors of q+1, it builds codes in every even dimension, and it uses the repeated-root factorization of x^n−1 to directly prove that no nontrivial MDS cyclic code exists when p divides n and n is not p.

entry.title: Deterministic design of polar subcodes using exact low-weight spectrum analysis
entry.summary: Deterministic Polar Subcode Design via Exact Low-Weight Spectrum Characterization arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper presents a deterministic framework that raises the minimum distance of polar subcodes by selecting information sets and designing frozen-bit expressions. It uses polar decomposition to compute the exact low-weight codeword spectrum and gives sufficient conditions for choosing coefficients sequentially. Experiments with block lengths from 64 to 1024 and several code rates report that the target minimum distances are reached within minutes, with competitive frame error rates under successive cancellation list decoding.

entry.title: Optimal square-root bound for online fair allocation of indivisible goods with known agent types
entry.summary: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies allocating indivisible goods to agents who arrive online and reveal one of k known additive valuation types, receiving irrevocable bundles immediately. The authors give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select, guaranteeing each agent about 1/√(2k) of their truncated proportional share, which dominates maximin share. They also tighten the upper bound to about √2/√k even for binary valuations, showing the optimal order is Θ(k^{-1/2}). Further exact results cover two arrivals, three arrivals with two types, and randomized policies. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an order-optimal Θ(k^{-1/2}) deterministic MMS bound via a polynomial-time algorithm, with tight bounds for two and three arrivals.

entry.title: Constant-factor single-sample prophet inequality for subadditive valuations
entry.summary: A Constant-Factor Single-Sample Prophet Inequality for Subadditive Valuations arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies online combinatorial allocation where buyers have monotone subadditive valuations and each buyer provides one independent sample from an unknown distribution. The authors give a reduction that turns any offline algorithm achieving an α fraction of optimal welfare into an online algorithm achieving an α/120 fraction of the expected offline optimum. The guarantee holds for arbitrary arrival orders and extends to the Game of Googol model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend single-sample prophet inequalities to monotone subadditive valuations, giving a reduction with a 1/120 constant factor for arbitrary arrival orders.

entry.title: Optimal signaling mechanisms for one-round matching markets
entry.summary: Optimal Signaling Mechanisms for One-round Matching Markets arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies signaling mechanisms in a one-round matching market with n applicants and n firms, where applicants signal interest in firms to improve matching outcomes. It considers a richer signal space than prior work and analyzes both deterministic and randomized mechanisms. In the limit as k grows, the optimal deterministic mechanism yields about 75.45% of applicants receiving offers, and the optimal randomized mechanism yields about 78.20%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors consider richer signal spaces and randomized signaling mechanisms, reporting optimal offer rates of about 75.45% deterministic and 78.20% randomized as k grows.

entry.title: Constructing ternary codes that correct two-symbol bursts perfectly
entry.summary: Ternary Perfect 2-Burst-Correcting Codes arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper presents a construction of ternary perfect linear 2-burst-correcting codes for every redundancy r≥5. The construction is recursive, with seed codes given for 5≤r≤7. Codes with redundancy r≥8 are derived from codes of redundancy r-3, with separate treatment for even and odd code lengths.

entry.title: Static detection of exactly-once violations in payment pipelines
entry.summary: The Defect Is in the Arithmetic Between the Files: Static Detection of Exactly-Once Violations in Payment Pipelines arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper argues that whether a streaming payment pipeline double-charges a customer after a restart depends on comparing how long a provider remembers an idempotency key with how stale a record can be when reprocessed, and these figures are scattered across separate files. The authors present a checker that gathers these facts and derives their relations, and a synthesiser that turns 335 of 515 findings into runnable replay scenarios. In live tests against a real Kafka broker with real process kills, all 16 selected witnesses reproduced their predicted outcomes, with 245 findings producing two charges. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors detect exactly-once violations by statically comparing idempotency-key lifetime with record staleness across files, reporting 16 live witnesses reproduced on real Kafka with process kills.

entry.title: RankServe: Rank-Aware CPU-GPU Scheduling for Memory-Limited MoE Model Serving
entry.summary: RankServe: Rank-Aware CPU-GPU Scheduling for Memory-Constrained MoE Serving arXiv · Nov 24, 2026RankServe is a CPU-GPU serving system for compressed Mixture-of-Experts models whose experts have different low-rank ranks. It estimates how much GPU residency saves compared with the cheaper CPU or transfer-then-GPU path, and keeps experts with the highest savings per byte on the GPU. Implemented on vLLM, it was evaluated on three MoE models against six serving systems, with reported geometric-mean speedups in TTFT and TPOT.

entry.title: Precoder optimization for mixed regular and wiretap coding with obfuscation
entry.summary: Multi-User Linear Precoder Optimization for Obfuscation-Aided Mixed Regular and Wiretap Coding arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes a generalized obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system built on a multi-user linear precoding architecture, which unifies existing approaches that use different obfuscation functions. The authors formulate a precoder optimization problem that abstracts the obfuscation function through a minimum secrecy rate constraint. Numerical simulations on a two-user line-of-sight channel show how this constraint sets the operating point between regular and wiretap coding, and that mixed coding allows individual beam shaping for each coding layer.

entry.title: Optimizing Movable-Antenna Paths and Power for Secure Transmission
entry.summary: Joint Trajectory and Power Optimization for Movable-Antenna-Aided Secure Transmission arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how a movable antenna can improve secure wireless transmission by sending signals while it moves. It maximizes the average secrecy rate under constraints on movement and transmit power, which are coupled over time. The authors separate the power and position variables using Lagrangian duality and a discretized linear rail, then apply a dual-based branch-and-bound algorithm. Simulation results indicate the proposed design outperforms benchmark schemes.

entry.title: Collateral Design and Correlated Slashing Risk in Liquid Restaking
entry.summary: Collateral Architecture and Correlated Slashing in Liquid Restaking arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies liquid restaking, where pooled stake secures several slashable commitments at once. It presents a unified model spanning unique stake and shared collateral, and shows that portfolio variance depends on gross exposure, concentration, and failure dependence. The authors analyze competing risk-sensitive allocators who receive rewards in proportion to committed exposure, establishing equilibrium properties. Reproducible synthetic stress tests are used to support the mechanisms.

entry.title: AeroPoint: Agentic AI for Intent-Driven Point Cloud Inspection in UAV-Edge Systems
entry.summary: AeroPoint: Agentic AI for Intent-Driven Point Cloud Inspection in UAV-Edge Systems arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents AeroPoint, a system for drone-based LiDAR inspection in which onboard processing builds a knowledge graph from point clouds. A large language model on a ground edge server turns natural-language inspection questions into structured requests, and the drone returns the matching graph evidence. The authors evaluate it on power line inspection using 150 TS40K UAV LiDAR scenes and measure processing costs on NVIDIA Jetson Nano hardware. Transmitted payload drops from 3700 KB to 3.1 KB, and the evaluated LLM routers achieve the highest graph retrieval completeness for relational queries.

entry.title: Real-time AI acceleration on a 2D spatial dataflow chip
entry.summary: Real-Time AI Acceleration on a 2D Spatial Dataflow Architecture arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies the timing analysis of the Tenstorrent Blackhole, a spatial dataflow AI accelerator built on a commodity RISC-V architecture with a 2D grid of cores connected by networks-on-chip. The authors profile the platform and build a worst-case execution time task model as a Homogeneous Synchronous Dataflow Graph, extended to multi-core workloads by accounting for NoC delays. Evaluated across 12,567 task configurations, the model's estimates lie above the observed worst case in every configuration.

entry.title: TokenJoule: Energy Modeling for Distributed LLM Training and Inference
entry.summary: TokenJoule: Energy Modeling for Distributed Training and Inference of LLMs arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents TokenJoule, an open-source analytical tool that predicts the energy use of large language model training and inference before hardware exists. It derives kernel sequences, tiled computation, shared-memory use, cache residency, and collective communication traffic, and prices each activity using component-level energy values. Without fitting to any workload, it reports 3.3-6.6% activity error across 151 A100/H100 runs and 3.0-6.8% energy error on A100.

entry.title: Predictive Self-Entropy in Dirichlet Coding: A Factor-Two Theorem
entry.summary: Predictive Self-Entropy in Dirichlet Universal Coding: A Factor-Two Central Limit Theorem and a Markov Extension arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies the Shannon entropy of the predictive distributions issued by sequential universal coders before each symbol is observed, comparing their cumulative sum with the realized arithmetic code length. For finite-alphabet memoryless sources and Dirichlet (add-α) predictors, the authors prove a joint central limit theorem for the two normalized quantities. Both share the same first-order entropy limit, but the cumulative predictive self-entropy has exactly twice the leading asymptotic variance of the code length. The result is extended to finite-order Markov sources via a context/innovation covariance decomposition.

entry.title: Single-photon detectors for optical wireless communication: a tutorial
entry.summary: Single-Photon Detectors for Optical Wireless Communications: A Tutorial arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This tutorial reviews single-photon detectors for optical wireless communication, comparing SPADs, silicon photomultipliers, CMOS SPAD arrays, superconducting nanowire detectors, and other technologies. It develops communication-level models for effects such as dead time, afterpulsing, crosstalk, and background counts, and links them to modulation, detection, synchronization, and decoding. The authors conclude that useful photon efficiency is an end-to-end property of the optical front end, detector, readout, and digital receiver rather than a detector metric alone.

entry.title: One-Release Private Simple Linear Regression Using an Improved Simplex Mapping
entry.summary: One Release for All: Private Simple Linear Regression Via Improved Simplex Mapping arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper extends DP-RSS to private simple linear regression for inputs and outputs bounded in [0,1]. Instead of releasing several related sufficient-statistic estimates separately, it encodes the needed information in a single unit-sensitivity vector and applies the Laplace mechanism once using the full privacy budget. The least-squares sufficient statistics are then recovered by deterministic post-processing. Reported variance reductions relative to DP-RSS range from 1.67 to 2.67 times for several statistics, with the largest benefit in the high-privacy regime.

entry.title: Computational complexity of concurrent stochastic games: exact values and approximation
entry.summary: The Computational Complexity of Concurrent Stochastic Games: Exact Value and Approximation arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies two-player zero-sum concurrent stochastic games on a finite state space played over infinitely many stages, with limit-average objectives for Player 1. It addresses two problems: approximating game values within an arbitrary additive error, and exactly deciding whether a state's value meets a given threshold. The authors show the approximation problem is in TFNP, with its gap version in NP ∩ coNP. They also show the exact problem lies in both the existential and universal theories of the reals and is PosSLP-hard. ★★★★ Notable: The paper studies limit-average values of two-player zero-sum concurrent stochastic games; the authors show the approximation problem lies in TFNP and its gap problem in NP∩coNP, and place the exact p

entry.title: Decoupling Faults from Uncertainty: Message-Efficient Byzantine Agreement with Local Predictions
entry.summary: Decoupling Faults from Uncertainty: Message-Efficient Byzantine Agreement with Local Predictions arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how much Byzantine Agreement can benefit when each process has a local bound on its failure-prediction error. It introduces a local k-error prediction model and presents a synchronous algorithm requiring n ≥ t + 4k + 1. When local uncertainty is small, the protocol's communication is decoupled from the total fault budget t, achieving o(n²) communication when t = Θ(n) and k = o(√n). The authors also show that at least Ω(nk) honest messages are necessary in this model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a local k-error prediction model, give a Byzantine agreement protocol with o(n²) communication, and report a matching Ω(nk) lower bound.

entry.title: Accurate Products, Inaccurate Inverse: Emulated FP64 Matrix Operations in Triangular Inversion
entry.summary: Accurate Products, Inaccurate Inverse: Emulated FP64 BLAS in Blocked Triangular Inversion arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper asks whether a blocked triangular inversion built from emulated FP64 matrix products keeps the accuracy of those products. The authors find that every product meets the standard error bound, yet the computed inverse is far less accurate than native FP64, because one product's summed index carries both a diagonal scaling and its inverse. Computing the problematic products natively restores accuracy, and the paper also presents equilibration, a solve-based reformulation, and an error recurrence for auditing runs. Speed comparisons on an RTX 4090 are included. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show per-product accuracy does not carry over to blocked triangular inversion, identify the culprit product, and report validation on four GPUs and real covariance matrices.

entry.title: Optimal matroid prophet inequality against all-knowing adversaries, and delegation
entry.summary: Optimal Matroid Prophets against Almighty Adversaries and Delegation arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper proves an optimal one-half matroid prophet inequality against an almighty adversary who sees all realized values before choosing the arrival order. The algorithm is deterministic: before values are revealed it partitions the ground set, replaces the matroid with a stricter direct sum of minors, fixes one threshold per part, and accepts greedily under these tests. The same construction yields a deterministic, agent-oblivious mechanism for matroid delegation with possibly correlated agent utilities, improving the guarantee from 1/4 to the optimal 1/2. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give a deterministic optimal 1/2 matroid prophet inequality against almighty adversaries, improving matroid delegation to 1/2 with tight bounds.

entry.title: Principal Revelations of the Revelation Principle: A Theory Paper on Mechanism Design
entry.summary: Principal Revelations of the Revelation Principle arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proves a converse to the revelation principle, showing it rests on an optimistic assumption: if it must hold in all environments, the principal must assume agents play her favorite equilibrium. When the principal knows only that the prior lies in some set, she must also assume that prior is her favorite one. With private values, independent types, and quasilinear payoffs, unrestricted transfers let the principal approximate any mechanism's equilibrium payoff using a direct mechanism whose unique equilibrium is truthful. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a converse to the revelation principle, showing it embeds optimism about equilibrium selection. With private values and transfers, a direct mechanism with unique truthful equilibrium

entry.title: Designing scoring rules that make risk-averse forecasters report honestly and gather information
entry.summary: Proper and Optimal Scoring Rules for Risk-Averse Agents arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies how to design scoring rules that pay agents based on their reported probabilities and realised outcomes, so that risk-averse agents report truthfully and are motivated to acquire costly information. For agents with entropic risk preferences over finite state spaces, it characterises proper scoring rules through an exponential transformation. It also derives optimal information-acquisition structures under bounded payments and gives explicit optimal coefficients in the binary case. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterise proper scoring rules for entropic risk-averse agents via exponential transformation and give explicit optimal coefficients in the binary case.

entry.title: Optimal XOR lemmas for information complexity
entry.summary: Optimal XOR Lemmas for Information Complexity arXiv · Nov 23, 2026Information complexity measures how much the parties to a communication protocol must reveal about their inputs to complete a task. This paper asks whether the information complexity of the XOR of n independent copies of a Boolean function obeys an XOR lemma, and fully resolves this for every error level from 0 to 1/3. For total functions, the result is Theta(n times the information complexity at error epsilon/n), except for degenerate functions of the form a(x) XOR b(y). The paper also characterizes partial functions and proves an optimal distributional XOR lemma and matching direct sum theorems. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve the open XOR lemma for information complexity, giving tight bounds across all error levels with matching direct sum theorems via information-theoretic and geometric methods.

entry.title: A deterministic protocol for envy-free cake cutting with polynomial queries
entry.summary: A Deterministic Polynomial-Query Protocol for Envy-Free Cake Cutting arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents a deterministic protocol that divides a heterogeneous cake completely and without envy among n agents, using O(n^6 log n) Robertson-Webb queries in the worst case. Valuations may be arbitrary nonnegative nonatomic measures, and each agent's bundle may be disconnected. The protocol makes O(n) calls to certified trimming, each using O(n^5 log n) queries. For complete envy-free chore allocation, the query bound is O(n^7 log n). ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a deterministic envy-free cake-cutting protocol with O(n^6 log n) Robertson-Webb queries, and extend the bound to chore allocation.

entry.title: Coarse Price Discrimination: Revenue Cost of Limiting Posted Prices
entry.summary: Coarse Price Discrimination arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how much revenue a seller loses when restricted to L posted prices, while heterogeneous buyers with independent values compete for scarce inventory. Under a large-market assumption, buyers are first made arbitrarily replaceable at fixed stock, and then stock is allowed to grow. In this limit, one price guarantees half of optimal mechanism revenue and two prices guarantee about 73.1%, with 1−1/(2L−1) for L≥3. The guarantees allow arbitrary demand differences across buyers and do not require a separate price for each customer group. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give large-market revenue guarantees for L posted prices: one price gets half of optimal revenue, two get about 73.1%, with a 1-1/(2L-1) bound for L≥3.

entry.title: Whether a Partition Bound for Multiterminal Secret Key Capacity Is Exact
entry.summary: Tightness of the Partition Bound for Multiterminal Secret Key Capacity arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies secret key agreement among m terminals who communicate over a public channel, with some terminals acting as helpers. It proves that the partition-based Csiszár–Narayan upper bound is tight for every source exactly when the target set size |A| is 2, m-2, m-1, or m, and extends a known six-terminal counterexample to the remaining cases. It also shows that for two target terminals on a connected Markov random field, an optimal bipartition can be chosen with both blocks connected, reducing candidate bipartitions on cycles from exponential to at most quadratic in m. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a complete characterization of when the partition bound is tight, extending Chan's counterexample, and report optimal bipartition structure on Markov random fields.

entry.title: Near-Isometric Embeddings of Graphs into Curved Surfaces and Network Coding
entry.summary: Almost-Isometric Embeddings of Graphs into Riemannian Manifolds arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies embedding the shortest-path metric of a finite weighted graph into a smooth closed surface. For any small ε>0, the authors construct a smooth closed orientable surface in ℝ³ that admits a noncontractive (1+ε)-embedding of the graph's vertices. The construction is also used to transfer network communication schemes between graphs and surfaces, comparing their coding advantages. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that any finite weighted graph embeds into a smooth closed surface with distortion approaching one, transferring coding advantage bounds between graphs and surfaces.

entry.title: Memory and query trade-offs in high-accuracy feasibility problems
entry.summary: Exponential memory/query-complexity tradeoffs in high-accuracy feasibility problems arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies the feasibility problem of finding a point inside a hidden small ball within the unit ball, given access to a separation oracle, focusing on very high accuracy. Previously known low-memory algorithms need query counts exponential in the dimension, but no nontrivial lower bound linking memory and queries existed. The authors prove that any algorithm using d^{1+δ}ln(1/ε) bits of memory requires at least (d ln(1/ε))^{Ω̃(d^{(1-δ)/8})} oracle calls. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a first non-trivial memory/query tradeoff lower bound for high-accuracy feasibility, exponential in dimension, matching known low-memory algorithms.

entry.title: Rateless Lattices: Constructions, Coding Theorems, and Capacity (rateless codes built from lattices that can keep producing symbols)
entry.summary: Rateless Lattices: Constructions, Coding Theorems, and Capacity arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper introduces rateless lattices, a sequence of growing integral lattices where each lattice projects onto the previous coordinates while keeping the finite codebook size constant. It gives a construction based on Construction D' with two nested Raptor codes, and proves a random-coding bound for multistage decoding. The authors show that stage-by-stage decoding causes a loss, and that joint decoding over a dense ensemble achieves the accumulated capacity of uniform pulse-amplitude modulation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce rateless lattice constructions and characterize their capacity region under joint decoding, with results covering multistage decoding loss and specific channel models.

entry.title: From Footprints to Service Regions: Modeling Dense LEO Satellite Networks
entry.summary: From Footprints to Service Regions: Modeling and Analysis of Dense LEO Satellite Networks Using an Orbit-Aware Cox Point Process arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies the service region of each satellite in dense low Earth orbit networks, meaning the set of locations it actually serves. Using an orbit-aware Cox point process on a common orbital shell, the authors model each service region as the intersection of a spherical-cap footprint and a spherical Voronoi cell under nearest-satellite association. Palm calculus yields exact expressions for mean area and perimeter and a coverage-load identity, which are connected to an approximate noise-limited user rate. The model is also compared with Starlink-type Walker constellations and reproduces their mean area and perimeter over broad latitude ranges. ★★★★ Notable: The authors model LEO service regions with an orbit-aware Cox process, derive exact mean area, perimeter and coverage-load expressions via Palm calculus, and compare against Walker constellations.

entry.title: Does Bragging Pay? A Study of Counterfactual Fair Credit Assignment
entry.summary: It Pays to Brag? On Counterfactual Fair Credit arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper examines how to assign credit for intellectual work such as software, legal documents, and scientific results, which can often be produced in several different ways. The authors generalize Shapley values to account for counterfactual ways of obtaining the same result. They show that fairness axioms including efficiency, nullity, and submodularity are incompatible with incentivizing creators to maximize social welfare. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize Shapley values to counterfactual ways of obtaining results, proving fairness axioms conflict with incentivizing welfare maximization.

entry.title: Finding Integral Stable Matchings Is PPAD-Complete
entry.summary: Finding Integral Stable Matchings is PPAD-Complete: Unimodular Hypergraphs, Network b-Matchings, and Kernels in Perfect Graphs arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies classical stability problems, including stable matchings in normal hypergraphs, stable b-matchings in unimodular hypergraphs, and kernels in perfect graphs, where polyhedral integrality guarantees integral stable solutions. The authors show that, unless PPAD is contained in FP, these solutions cannot be computed efficiently. Finding a stable matching is already PPAD-complete in linear unimodular hypergraphs with hyperedges of size at most three and vertex degrees at most three. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show finding integral stable matchings is PPAD-complete on linear unimodular hypergraphs and perfect-graph kernels, answering open questions via constant-size gadget reductions.

entry.title: Adaptive beamforming using one-bit data samples to estimate covariance
entry.summary: Adaptive Beamforming Using One-Bit Data Samples for Covariance Estimation arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how one-bit quantized complex data samples can be used to compute an array's data covariance, reducing computational complexity in distributed settings. The covariance estimate is applied to adaptive beamforming, and two approaches are presented: a covariance matrix built from one-bit samples, and a hybrid cross-covariance between one-bit and full-precision data. The authors derive signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) estimates for population and finite-sample matrices and compare them with full-precision results. The analysis assumes several strong, well-separated interferers with little overlap with the signal of interest, none of them dominant.

entry.title: Geometry and reliability of a recursive fractal peer-to-peer network design
entry.summary: Geometry, Reliability, and Spacetime Dynamics of Hyper-Simplex Fractal Networks arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper proposes a hyper-simplex fractal network G(N,m), a recursive topology that unifies naming, routing, consensus, and ordering in peer-to-peer systems. Nodes determine adjacency and forward messages along exact shortest paths using only digit-word addresses, without routing tables. Hierarchical PBFT consensus on the same structure is shown to have linear message load and logarithmic fault-free latency, with an explicit reliability threshold under independent faults.

entry.title: X-BQSR: Speeding Up Genomic Base Quality Recalibration Across GPUs
entry.summary: X-BQSR: Holistic Acceleration of Base Quality Recalibration for Scalable Genomic Analysis arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines base quality score recalibration (BQSR), a costly step in the GATK genomics pipeline that corrects systematic sequencing errors. The authors find that offloading only key stages to a GPU does not yield overall gains, so they redesign the entire pipeline, including I/O, compression, and kernel execution. The implementation uses portable SYCL kernels, with CUDA and HIP backends for comparison. The authors report up to 141.7x acceleration over standard GATK and up to 8.7x over a proprietary GPU-accelerated solution.

entry.title: Information-theoretic generalization bounds for adaptive learning under privacy and fairness constraints
entry.summary: Information-Theoretic Generalization for Adaptive Learning Under Privacy and Fairness Constraints arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how adaptive learners that repeatedly examine the same data generalize when privacy and fairness constraints limit information only about a sensitive coordinate, while task loss depends on a different coordinate. It defines a residual-information certificate, a chain-rule transfer inequality, and a transcript-level composition theorem for sequential learners. The results are applied to selective privacy and fairness settings, and FRL, EFRL, SFRL and ESFRL constructions are used to study the tightness of the task-information upper bounds.

entry.title: SYCLDB: A Database Engine Running on GPUs from Multiple Vendors
entry.summary: SYCLDB: A Cross-Vendor Heterogeneous Analytical DBMS arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents SYCLDB, an analytical database engine built on the open SYCL standard. Core relational operators are implemented as modular SYCL kernels and connected to a SQL frontend based on Apache Calcite and Apache Thrift, with Apache Arrow used for columnar data ingestion. The authors report that a single SYCL codebase can run analytical query pipelines on Intel, AMD, and NVIDIA GPUs, reducing reliance on vendor-specific GPU programming stacks.

entry.title: Which ◇P Algorithm Fits Your Needs? A Benchmark on Real Network Traces
entry.summary: Which Diamond P Algorithm is Suitable for You? An Empirical Benchmark on Real Network Traces arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper reviews 14 ◇P and closely related unreliable failure detectors for distributed systems, implementing 13 of them. It compares them using quality-of-service metrics such as detection time, mistake rate, and query accuracy, combining network trace replay with live deployment. The authors frame detector selection as a constrained algorithm-selection problem and find that no detector is uniformly best across the tested settings. At relaxed detection-time budgets, 2W is selected most often.

entry.title: Constrained-Support Local Randomizers for Robust Private Distribution Learning
entry.summary: Support-Constrained Local Randomizers for Robust Private Distribution Learning arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies local randomizers that restrict reports to input neighborhoods, reducing reporting distortion while introducing support mismatch. Under range-restricted approximate local differential privacy, the authors decompose the exact privacy defect into support leakage and overlap excess loss, and solve the privacy-distortion problem in closed form for line-supported sparse randomized response. For distribution estimation, they derive an exact finite-sample risk identity and analyze least-favorable distributions and minimax risk on cyclic alphabets.

entry.title: Torcalia.jl: An MPI-based Julia runtime for asynchronous task parallelism
entry.summary: Torcalia.jl: An MPI-based Runtime System for Asynchronous Task Parallelism in Julia arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents Torcalia.jl, a Julia package that orchestrates asynchronous task execution across shared and distributed memory systems, built on MPI.jl and Julia's native multithreading. It uses a dependency-aware scheduler combining work-sharing and work-stealing for adaptive load balancing, and supports arbitrarily nested tasks and application-level distributed shared memory. Evaluated on the ARIS supercomputer with four workloads, it reduced wall-clock time by up to 18.1% compared with Dagger, a Julia task-based engine.

entry.title: A variant of the Erdős–Gyárfás problem for K_9 and K_12
entry.summary: A variant of the Erdős--Gyárfás problem for K₉ and K₁₂ arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies edge-colorings of complete graphs in which every copy of a given graph H contains a color used an odd number of times, with r_H(n) denoting the minimum number of colors needed. The authors prove that r_{K_9}(n) and r_{K_12}(n) are both at most exp(O((log n)^{2/3})). These bounds yield linear graph codes of density at least exp(-O((log n)^{2/3})) that avoid images of K_9 and K_12.

entry.title: Stay or Switch? Metric Distortion When Candidates Arrive Online
entry.summary: Stay or Switch? Metric Distortion with Online Candidate Arrivals arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies metric distortion in sequential elections where candidates arrive one at a time. Each round, a new challenger faces the incumbent, and a voting rule picks one of the two based on voters' pairwise preferences. For deterministic rules, the authors show an asymptotically optimal distortion of Θ(√t) at round t. Randomized rules achieve constant distortion, with persistent randomized dictatorship reaching optimal distortion 5 against adaptive adversaries and 3 against oblivious ones.

entry.title: A pipeline-parallel system for models that loop through their layers
entry.summary: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models arXiv · Nov 23, 2026Depth-recurrent (looped) models reuse a shared stack of blocks several times to increase effective depth. The paper argues that the common interleaved 1F1B pipeline schedule assumes an acyclic stage graph, so splitting a looped model causes repeated stage visits and out-of-order communication that can stall. The authors present Loop-PP, which redesigns the schedule and communication for this cyclic layout and emits a static per-rank instruction stream that overlaps communication with compute. On 8B to 60B MoE models it reduces peak memory by up to 32.8%, and at fixed compute budget raises the best observed throughput by 12.7%.

entry.title: What information is preserved in authenticated Byzantine communication?
entry.summary: What Information Survives Authenticated Byzantine Communication? arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies two principals who independently approve actions that a delegate carries out under current policy, with a receipt recording the routes authorized at issuance. For intersection policies, it characterizes the leading number of reachable joint configurations under overlapping updates and gives a matching protocol. Worked examples of three-command workflows compute these counts and the bits needed per block under different overwrite encodings.

entry.title: CGSpec: Consistency-guided speculative decoding with overlap-aware scheduling for edge-cloud AI inference
entry.summary: CGSpec: Consistency-Guided Speculative Decoding with Overlap-Aware Verification Scheduling for Edge-Cloud Inference arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents CGSpec, a framework that speeds up large language model inference in edge-cloud setups, where edge devices draft tokens and a cloud model verifies them. It adjusts the speculative budget based on how much the draft and target model distributions diverge, and builds candidate token trees through a nomination and competition mechanism. An overlap-aware scheduler estimates remaining verification work and client return times to prioritize requests. Across 24 configurations with 8 and 16 clients, the authors report higher system and client throughput than prior methods.

entry.title: Cross-correlation of binary sequences and related constacyclic codes
entry.summary: Cross Correlation of Binary Niho-type Sequences and Related Constacyclic Codes arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies the cross correlation between a binary m-sequence of length q^2-1 and its d-decimated sequence, where q=2^m and m is an odd integer at least 3. The authors prove the cross correlation takes exactly four values and determine its distribution. For shift-decimated sequences, at most five values arise. The value distribution of associated exponential sums is also determined, and these results are used to construct q-ary constacyclic codes and find their weight distributions.

entry.title: One Structure Is Enough: Record-Native Tiles for Evolving Sparse Matrices on GPUs
