entry.summary: One Structure Is Enough: Record-Native Tiles for Evolving Sparse Matrices on GPUs arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents RecTile, a tiled storage layer for sparse matrices that change over time, keeping each tile in a single sorted array of 12-byte edge records. On fragmented matrices it runs in 0.56 to 1.21 times the time of the best format-pinned slab tile. A fully GPU-based ingest pipeline applies update batches at up to 29 million edges per second.

entry.title: Lee-weight distributions of various defining sets over the mixed-alphabet ring Z₂^α Z₄^β
entry.summary: Various Kinds of Defining Sets over ℤ₂^αℤ₄^β and their Lee-Weight Distributions arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies Lee-weight distributions associated with ten kinds of defining sets, labelled A to J, for code constructions over the mixed-alphabet ring Z₂^α Z₄^β. The authors use Parseval's identity to determine the cardinalities of these defining sets. They also present several new results on 2-Lee-weight and 3-Lee-weight distributions.

entry.title: MotionServe: Efficient Shared-GPU Serving for Many Robot Policies
entry.summary: MotionServe: Efficient Multi-Robot Serving by Exploiting Robot Execution Slack arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents MotionServe, a shared-GPU serving system that runs inference for many task-specific vision-language-action robot policies at once. It lets policies share a frozen backbone through LoRA adapters, chooses observation timing from the motion structure of predicted action chunks, and decides batching and dispatch using each robot's remaining execution slack and outstanding GPU work. On LIBERO and SimplerEnv tasks with 96 simulated robots sharing one H200 GPU, mean stall per episode drops by 43.4% and 32.6%, and task success improves by 8.98 and 2.30 percentage points.

entry.title: Whether self-orthogonal MDS codes exist for given length and dimension
entry.summary: On Self-orthogonal MDS Codes arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies the existence of self-orthogonal MDS codes, which are codes that are self-orthogonal and meet the Singleton bound. The authors fully resolve the problem for even prime power q except the case [q+2,3], and solve several cases for odd q. They use algebraic geometry codes, where choosing an appropriate differential gives explicit constructions.

entry.title: CSI-free end-to-end neural decoding of LDPC codes under synchronization errors
entry.summary: CSI-Agnostic End-to-End Neural Decoding of LDPC Codes under Synchronization Errors arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper proposes ASDecoder, a data-driven neural decoder for LDPC codes over insertion-deletion-substitution channels that does not require explicit channel state information. It combines a CNN-Transformer front-end for implicit sequence alignment with a syndrome-free BiDecoder back-end that avoids intermediate hard decisions. Experiments report that a single ASDecoder outperforms the BCJRFormer baseline and generalizes to the CCSDS (128,64) QC-LDPC standard and DNA constraints.

entry.title: New evidence for a conjecture on list recoverability of folded Reed–Solomon codes
entry.summary: Evidence Toward a Conjecture in List Recoverability of Folded Reed--Solomon Codes arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies the list-recoverability of folded Reed–Solomon codes and gives new evidence for a conjecture by Chen and Zhang (STOC 2025) that a certain upper bound is tight. The authors prove that explicit folded Reed–Solomon codes with rates arbitrarily close to (a−1)/(a+ℓ−2) are (0,ℓ,L)-list-recoverable, confirming the conjecture when ρ=0 and ℓ=2. They also show that for any rate R in (0,(a−1)/a), attaining the conjectured bound at rates close to R requires exponentially large alphabets.

entry.title: Selling Training Data: Why One Posted Price Can Be Optimal When Buyers Merge Datasets
entry.summary: Selling Training Data arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies how to sell supplementary training data to improve a predictive model. The buyer holds private knowledge of its own dataset and can choose how to merge it with the purchased one, which imposes a new constraint: the buyer's total net utility must be monotonic in the Blackwell order on private datasets. Under a differential virtual-value condition, the authors show that a single posted price for a fully informative dataset is optimal in hypothesis testing. The result extends to multi-class classification, where private datasets share a clean component but differ in how their labels are contaminated.

entry.title: Linear codes built from weight functions of three-weight codes
entry.summary: Several families of linear codes via weight functions of three-weight codes arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper extends a framework that builds new linear codes from a given code using weight functions, moving from two-weight codes to three-weight codes. It uses a known family of ternary three-weight cyclic codes and determines the weight distribution of every codimension-one subcode along with the distribution of fixed-weight codewords across them. This yields three classes of linear codes with four nonzero weights, whose parameters are explicitly determined. The codes are also shown to be self-orthogonal and minimal.

entry.title: Measuring GPU Memory Traffic on NVIDIA GB10 Without C2C Telemetry
entry.summary: Measuring GPU Memory Traffic on the NVIDIA GB10 Without C2C Telemetry arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper addresses how to measure traffic between the GPU and CPU-attached LPDDR5X memory over the C2C link on the NVIDIA GB10, where no software counter is exposed. It samples five GPU L2 sector counters every 10 ms via CUPTI to measure memory traffic live and separate copy engine traffic from kernel read misses and writes. The authors report close agreement with the expected volume for large streaming transfers on two systems, and show Mistral 7B decode reading 13.47 GiB per token at 83% of specified bandwidth. The method is released as open source.

entry.title: G-Wave: a generative method that turns bits into adaptive wireless waveforms
entry.summary: G-Wave: Bit-to-Waveform Generation for Adaptive Wireless Communications arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper introduces G-Wave, a channel-conditioned generative transceiver that synthesizes environment-adaptive physical time-domain waveforms directly from bits. Its Transformer-based transmitter and receiver use a multiscale architecture and are jointly trained end-to-end using only bit-reconstruction error, without waveform labels. Across diverse 3GPP wireless environments with estimated channel information, G-Wave reduces mean BER by 42.4% compared with DeepOFDM and by 72.6% compared with OFDM.

entry.title: Computational cost of iterated full-information protocols
entry.summary: The Complexity of Full-Information Iterated Protocols arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies iterated full-information protocols in distributed computing, where processes share their entire knowledge each round, usually assumed to carry unbounded information. The authors limit each process to sharing at most b bits with every other process per round and analyze the cost of simulating r iterations. For a large family of shared-memory models with n+1 processes, they prove a lower bound of Ω((n!)^(r-1) 2^(n-b)) rounds. They also give simulations that are asymptotically optimal in the conventional read-write model. The two-process case is special, needing only r rounds and 2-bit variables.

entry.title: Loop-free routing tree updates: why even two rounds are hard
entry.summary: Two Rounds Are Already Hard for Loop-Free Updates of Routing Trees arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies how to update routing trees in rounds without creating loops, requiring every partial completion of an update to remain acyclic. It shows that deciding whether two update rounds suffice is NP-complete, even when a safe three-round schedule is provided. The proof is a linear-size reduction from 3-SAT that uses mixed cycles to enforce consistent variable choices and clause satisfaction.

entry.title: Less Rational, More Transparent: Censorship as Optimal Disclosure
entry.summary: Less Rational, More Transparent: Censorship as (Robustly) Optimal Disclosure arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper studies how platforms should disclose information to boundedly rational users who follow the logit quantal response model, where the platform may not know their rationality level. It finds that censorship-style disclosure, which pools all sufficiently favorable options under a common message and reveals the rest individually, remains optimal or robustly optimal whether rationality is known or uncertain. The authors conclude that platforms should keep badge-based disclosure but narrow its pooling coverage to be more transparent.

entry.title: Motivo: Faster, More Energy-Efficient Genome Graph Read Mapping via Motif-Based Co-Design
entry.summary: Motivo: A Motif-Based Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Fast and Energy-Efficient Graph-Based Genome Analysis arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper addresses the bottleneck of mapping sequenced genome reads to genome graphs, which represent genetic diversity as alternative paths. It proposes Motivo, which precomputes recurring small subgraph patterns called motifs into a compact index and uses them to select a few suitable mapping paths, along with a co-designed accelerator, Motivo-ASIC. The authors report speedups over several existing CPU, GPU, and hardware tools, along with higher throughput per Watt and per mm² than SeGraM and HARP, while keeping mapping accuracy at 96.8%–99.7%.

entry.title: CXL coherence writes modified lines back before other hosts read them, so flushes are needed only for ordering
entry.summary: CXL Coherence Writes Back What Surviving Hosts See, Leaving Flushes Only for Ordering arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies data safety in multi-host systems sharing memory over CXL when one host crashes. The authors argue that when the crashed host's clients die with it, the flushes needed after a host crash are those that order lines on the memory device, not those that make completed operations durable. Their argument rests on CXL's requirement that a modified line is written back before another host accesses it. The claim is proved for single-store operations and tested on small models of three published designs, including a persistent hash index that writes fewer lines in two workloads.

entry.title: Best odd unimodular lattices in dimensions 49 to 59
entry.summary: Optimal odd unimodular lattices in dimensions 49 through 59 arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper shows that the largest minimum norm of unimodular lattices is 4 in dimension 49 and 5 in dimensions 50, 51, 57 and 58. It also studies the theta series of optimal unimodular lattices in each dimension from 49 to 59. In dimensions 50, 51 and 57, the first known unimodular lattices with minimum norm 5 are obtained from self-dual codes via Construction A.

entry.title: LiZoneDedup: An End-to-End In-Storage Deduplication Architecture for ZNS SSDs
entry.summary: LiZoneDedup: An End-to-End In-Storage Deduplication Architecture for ZNS SSDs arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper presents LiZoneDedup, described as the first complete in-storage deduplication architecture for Zoned Namespace (ZNS) SSDs. It exploits ZNS's append-only contract, storing dedup metadata as an append-only log and compact per-zone fingerprint indexes instead of a global page-level table. On a 1 TB ZNS SSD, the design improves logical write throughput by 1.1 to 3.5 times and cuts physical writes by up to 85%, while keeping controller DRAM at 37 to 50 MB.

entry.title: Detecting hidden linear links between shuffled data pairs
entry.summary: The broken-sample problem revisited II: Detecting hidden linear dependencies arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies whether covariates and responses in a regression setting are independent or linked by a hidden permutation followed by a linear relationship. The authors identify detection thresholds in low dimensions and propose moment-based test statistics, inspired by matched filters, that run in nearly linear time. For higher dimensions, tests based on sliced Wasserstein distance succeed under a stated noise condition, while the optimal threshold remains open.

entry.title: Denoising Full-Rank Matrices Under Non-Gaussian Random Noise
entry.summary: Extensive-Rank Matrix Denoising Under i.i.d. Non-Gaussian Noise arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies removing noise from full-rank, rotationally invariant matrix signals corrupted by i.i.d. non-Gaussian noise. It uses an orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP) algorithm that alternates between a spectral estimator and an entrywise denoiser. The authors conjecture a Gaussian equivalence property and derive a state evolution recursion for the effective noise variances. Simulations show the predictions closely match empirical errors, and for robust PCA, OAMP recovers a larger region than several existing methods.

entry.title: Minimizing the Cramér-Rao Bound in Discrete SIM-Aided Integrated Sensing and Communication
entry.summary: Cramer-Rao Bound Minimization for Discrete SIM-aided ISAC Systems arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies how to minimize the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB), a limit on estimation accuracy, in an integrated sensing and communication system that uses discrete stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM). The authors propose a two-stage transmit design: an ideal precoder is first computed, then realized on a practical multi-layer SIM by alternating power allocation and phase-shift updates with closed-form discrete projection. Numerical results show fast convergence, a sensing-communication trade-off, and CRB improvements with higher phase resolution and larger SIM configurations.

entry.title: Ossim: OS-Driven Live Simulation for Full-Stack Evaluation of Clusters (Extended Version)
entry.summary: Ossim: OS-Driven Live Simulation for Cluster-Scale Full-Stack Evaluation (Extended Version) arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper presents Ossim, an OS-level approach to cluster-scale full-stack simulation built on the Linux virtualization stack. It aims to evaluate distributed software stacks and emerging hardware components before deployment. Ossim has four subsystems: simulation-oriented scheduling, live memory hierarchy management, simulation-aware IPC, and multi-host coordination. Together they coordinate live and modeled components under shared simulated time while controlling interference among co-located live VMs.

entry.title: When Does Splitting LLM Serving Help? A Workload-Architecture Study
entry.summary: When Does Decomposition Help? Empirical Study on Workload-Architecture Affinity in LLM Inference Serving arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper compares five SGLang serving setups for large language model inference on the same four-A100-40GB hardware, using a fixed Qwen3-8B model and identical prompts and arrival schedules. Across 150 audited test conditions, four independent single-GPU replicas gave the lowest end-to-end latency for short chat and long output and were stable in every condition. Pipeline parallelism cut time to first token for 32K-token prompts by 58-59% at non-stress rates. The authors conclude that splitting serving into parts helps only when the split matches the workload's dominant phase.

entry.title: Fluid-antenna-assisted cancellation of self-interference in full-duplex radios (FAS-SIM)
entry.summary: FAS-Assisted Self-Interference Mitigation for In-Band Full-Duplex Communications arXiv · Nov 22, 2026In-band full-duplex communication must cancel strong self-interference from the device's own transmission. This paper proposes FAS-SIM, a pilot-efficient method that selects the fluid antenna system port using only the loopback self-interference channel, without requiring forward channel state information. The authors provide a theoretical performance analysis of the forward signal. Numerical results show that FAS-SIM achieves self-interference suppression and forward-link rate comparable to the conventional method while reducing port-selection training overhead by 50%.

entry.title: Achievable rate and reconstruction quality of FeFET-based in-pixel computing arrays
entry.summary: Achievable Rate and Reconstruction Fidelity of FeFET-Based Compute-in-Pixel Arrays arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies compute-in-pixel image sensors such as MACPix, which weight each pixel's photodiode voltage by a conductance stored in a ferroelectric FET and sum the currents on a column bus. The authors model the bus as a Gaussian multiple-access channel and derive its achievable rate under thermal and shot noise, device variation, and ADC distortion. They report a limit of 4.5 bits per readout, with a 6-bit ADC being sufficient. End-to-end simulations recover natural images at 26.3 dB from 2 bits per pixel.

entry.title: Stackelberg Games Evaluated with Convex Risk Measures
entry.summary: Stackelberg Games with Convex Risk Measures arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies finite Stackelberg games where environmental uncertainty makes each strategy profile yield a random reward, which players assess using convex risk measures. It gives two conditions under which the follower has a unique continuous mixed response, and shows that even approximately computing an equilibrium is NP-hard. The authors derive an exact mathematical program with equilibrium constraints and propose an entropy-smoothed implicit-gradient method, validated by experiments on synthetic and real data.

entry.title: Privacy-preserving semantic communication using federated learning and knowledge-enhanced networks
entry.summary: Semantic Communication via Federated Learning with Knowledge-Enhanced Networks and Privacy arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper proposes a privacy-preserving semantic communication framework that combines federated learning with knowledge-enhanced networks for distributed wireless systems. Clients collaboratively train a model without sharing their data or knowledge graphs, using a multi-objective optimization balancing semantic fidelity, knowledge integration, channel robustness, and reconstruction accuracy. Numerical results under AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels show the multi-client approach outperforms single-client and centralized baselines at all SNRs, with the largest gains at low SNR.

entry.title: Last-iterate convergence of payoff-gradient learning in Möbius pricing games
entry.summary: Last-Iterate Convergence of Payoff-Gradient Learning in Möbius Pricing Games arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper proves that payoff-gradient learning converges globally in its last iterate, with explicit rates, across a class of Bayesian bidding and pricing games. The class covers first-price auctions, unit-demand pay-as-bid auctions, rank-based generalized first-price auctions, and homogeneous-good price competition with inelastic demand. The convergence holds for symmetric self-play from any continuous weakly increasing feasible initial strategy.

entry.title: Low-latency layered MLSE design for PAM4 short-reach optical links
entry.summary: Layered soft-output MLSE architecture for PAM4 short-reach optical interconnects arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper proposes a layered soft-output maximum-likelihood sequence estimation (SMLSE) architecture for high-speed data-center optical interconnects. It reduces latency from linear to logarithmic order by combining interval metrics in parallel and reconstructing state metrics at interval midpoints. In 112-Gbit/s PAM4 experiments over 2 km of standard single-mode fiber, the layered design matched conventional SMLSE soft-output performance while cutting total latency from 26 to 10 processing cycles.

entry.title: Simplified Plotkin-type bounds for function-correcting codes under b-symbol and sum-rank distances
entry.summary: Simplified Plotkin-type Bounds for Function-Correcting Codes with b-Symbol and Sum-Rank Distances arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies function-correcting codes, which allow recovery of specific functions of transmitted messages with minimal redundancy, under the b-symbol and sum-rank distances. Existing general Plotkin-type bounds on optimal redundancy require computing pairwise distances between vectors mapped to different function values, which is often computationally difficult. The authors derive simplified bounds that depend only on the number of message vectors per function value and the sum of pairwise distances among vectors mapped to the same value, and these apply to arbitrary functions. The known simplified bounds for linear functions are included as special cases, and a tighter bound for linear functions under the sum-rank distance is obtained.

entry.title: Proof of a Conjecture on Codes Without Self-Overlap
entry.summary: A Proof of Blackburn's Conjecture on Non-Overlapping Codes arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies non-overlapping codes, in which no nonempty proper prefix of a codeword is also a suffix of a codeword. It proves Blackburn's conjecture that, for every length n and all sufficiently large alphabet sizes q, the best code of the form I^{n-1}J is a maximum non-overlapping code. The proof uses generating functions for the nested partitions that describe maximal non-overlapping codes. The paper also shows that only these codes with |I|=(n-1)q/n, and their reversals, meet Levenshtein's bound.

entry.title: R2WM: A recursive reasoning wireless model for predicting millimeter-wave beams far into the future
entry.summary: R2WM: Recursive Reasoning Wireless Model for Long-Horizon mmWave Beam Prediction arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper proposes R2WM, a recursive reasoning wireless model for long-horizon beam prediction in mobile millimeter-wave systems. It takes a fixed history of beam indices and angles of departure, repeatedly updates coupled latent and prediction states with a shared causal-attention backbone, and then jointly decodes future beam indices. In the standard 10-step DeepMIMO setting, it reaches an average normalized beamforming gain of 0.9597, versus 0.8629 for a prompt-as-prefix large language model, with 99.1% fewer parameters.

entry.title: IndexerStage: Staging Indexer-K State Across Memory Tiers for Sparse-Attention LLM Serving
entry.summary: IndexerStage: Staging Indexer-K across Memory Tiers for Sparse-Attention LLM Serving arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper addresses GPU memory limits in long-context sparse-attention LLM serving, where the Indexer-K state grows with input length. It presents IndexerStage, a serving runtime that moves this state to a backing memory tier, staging completed pages through shared buffers while keeping new entries local. Implemented in SGLang on H800 GPUs, it increases batch size by 12.28% to 23.08% over host-memory-backed HiSparse and reaches 1.08x to 1.14x decode throughput.

entry.title: Speeding Up Repeated Variational Circuit Optimization on GPUs
entry.summary: Making Repeated Variational Circuit Optimization Efficient on GPUs arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper addresses classical simulation of parameterized quantum circuits, noting that training steps change gate parameters while keeping circuit connectivity and reusing a few gate-layer patterns. The authors propose a GPU framework that combines execution primitives for common circuit layers with adjoint differentiation to speed up gradient evaluation. It selects execution plans by narrowing options under structural and hardware constraints and measuring representative layers, then reuses those plans while the circuit structure stays fixed. Experiments across several circuit families and GPU platforms compare it with PennyLane Lightning's native GPU adjoint implementation, reporting substantially lower gradient evaluation times and numerical accuracy checks.

entry.title: CCAMoE: Cache-Conditioned Adaptive Inference for Offloaded Mixture-of-Experts Models
entry.summary: CCAMoE: Cache-Conditioned Adaptive Inference for Offloaded MoE arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper presents CCAMoE, a runtime that speeds up decoding for Mixture-of-Experts models whose experts are offloaded on memory-limited GPUs. It drafts tokens using already-resident target experts instead of separate draft weights, and updates the expert cache in step with drafting and verification so transfers overlap computation. It also adjusts draft length based on expected acceptance versus execution cost. The authors report the lowest decoding latency across various models, GPUs, and workloads, with up to 2.33× speedup over state-of-the-art baselines.

entry.title: Hierarchical beam training for flexible metasurfaces in hybrid near- and far-field multiuser communication
entry.summary: Hierarchical Sub-Array Beam Training for Flexible Intelligent Metasurface-Enabled Hybrid Near-Far-Field Multiuser Communications arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper addresses beam pattern distortion caused by low-resolution discrete phase shifters in extremely large arrays by using flexible intelligent metasurface shaping as an extra geometric beamforming degree of freedom. It models the hybrid near-field and far-field channel and beam patterns, and proposes a hierarchical sub-array beam training scheme that progressively enlarges the activated aperture and selects codewords adaptively. Simulations show beam patterns comparable to continuous-phase designs, lower training overhead, and higher multiuser sum rates than conventional rigid-array benchmarks.

entry.title: Mechanism Design under Belief Disagreement: Allocation Flexibility and Rent Capacity
entry.summary: Mechanism Design under Belief Disagreement: Allocation Flexibility and Rent Capacity arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies how a seller jointly chooses allocations and payments when buyers misperceive competition. Under independent private values and payment restrictions, the allocation determines both the rents required and the capacity to deliver them. The authors give explicit conditions for optimal lower-value lotteries under shared-top beliefs and show a strict allocation advantage over reserve prices in a two-buyer construction. They also identify when objective-law revenue ceilings are restored and estimate, using scaled public auction records, the recurring costs such redesigns can cover.

entry.title: Asynchronous uplink rate-splitting multiple access: sending two users' signals in layers with timing offsets
entry.summary: Asynchronous Uplink Rate Splitting Multiple Access arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies a two-user uplink system in which each user splits its message into layers sent with deliberately chosen timing offsets, a scheme called asynchronous rate splitting (A-RS). It shows that the offsets make the layers distinguishable only in the excess band of the pulse and gives a closed-form rate expression. By using excess bandwidth that synchronous transmission leaves unused, A-RS achieves rate pairs outside the regions of both synchronous and asynchronous non-orthogonal multiple access.

entry.title: A Softmax Method for Splitting a Player's Standing Across Several Groups
entry.summary: A Characterized Softmax for Distributing Standing Across Multiple Affiliations arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies cooperative games where players belong to several overlapping groups, and asks how a player's standing should be divided among those groups. It shows that a simple ratio-based answer fails when a player's group signals have mixed signs, and proposes a restricted-domain softmax construction instead. The authors prove that, under a defined richness condition on the group structure, this map is the unique one satisfying five requirements up to a temperature parameter. A worked example on an exact cooperative game checks these requirements numerically.

entry.title: Adaptive Keep-Alive Control to Reduce Serverless Cold Starts
entry.summary: Adaptive Warm-State Retention for Serverless Cold-Start Mitigation: Treating Keep-Alive Time as an Online Control Parameter arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper addresses cold-start latency in serverless platforms, which occurs when idle function environments must be rebuilt before serving a request. It proposes treating the keep-alive window as a per-function parameter adjusted online, separate from replica count. The authors build an external controller for OpenFaaS/faasd using an AIMD rule and a UCB1 multi-armed bandit, and compare it with fixed-timeout and predictive histogram baselines. The bandit reduces the cold-start rate from 63% under immediate scale-to-zero to 3%, while keeping P95 tail latency near the longest fixed baseline with about 13% less warm time.

entry.title: Live migration of streaming DeltaNet requests and the cost of log backlog
entry.summary: GDNShift: Live Migration and Joint State Scheduling for Gated DeltaNet Inference arXiv · Nov 19, 2026The paper studies how to live-migrate a streaming Gated DeltaNet (GDN) request by recovering its recurrent state at the correct token boundary on a worker with the same model weights. It combines snapshots, batched replay, and token catch-up, and proposes a compact update-log migration path. In 1,350 pure-GDN trials on two GPU deployments, compact logs gave the shortest exact handoff gap in all 90 configurations, while exact catch-up always released the source earliest and 32-step replay gave the highest output rate when arithmetic differences were allowed.

entry.title: Asymptotic limits for codes under toroidal distance
entry.summary: Asymptotic Bounds for Codes in Toroidal Distance arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper studies asymptotic bounds for codes in Z_q^n under the toroidal metric, where distances are measured modulo q. Using the classical Gilbert–Varshamov bounds for Hamming and Lee metrics as a baseline, it derives an asymptotic Gilbert–Varshamov lower bound and a Hamming-type upper bound via a saddle-point approach. For 3 dividing q, it embeds ternary Hamming codes to obtain another lower bound. It also gives an asymptotic lower bound for Maximum Toroidal Distance (MTD) codes and compares the bounds numerically. Correction Nov 24, 2026: Marked withdrawn by its source; no longer a pick

entry.title: TripleKV: A three-tier KV cache system that prefetches agent cache data before it is needed
entry.summary: TripleKV: Predict, Prefetch, Protect - KV Cache Management for AI Agents arXiv · Nov 19, 2026This paper addresses the problem that AI agents, which alternate between model inference and tool calls, accumulate key-value (KV) caches too large for GPU memory under high concurrency. TripleKV predicts when tool calls will finish using a tool-aware latency predictor and prefetches the needed KV blocks from SSD into host DRAM in advance. It also removes duplicate blocks between GPU and DRAM and refills evicted GPU blocks from SSD through a victim-cache mechanism. The reported results show that the share of requests needing critical-path SSD reads falls from 45–76% to under 10%, and P95 time to first token drops by up to 49%.

entry.title: An Upper Bound on Non-Overlapping Codes
entry.summary: A tight upper bound on non-overlapping codes arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies binary non-overlapping codes, also called bifix-free or strong comma-free codes, which have been examined in information theory for over 60 years. It gives a self-contained proof that, as code length n grows, the number of codewords is bounded by (5/(6e)+O(n^{-1}))·2^n/n. This improves the previous best bound by Levenshtein (1970) by a factor of 5/6.

entry.title: Artificial Currency and Separate Selling: A 3-Approximation for Consumer Surplus
entry.summary: Artificial Currency and Separate Selling: A Constant Approximation for Consumer Surplus arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how to allocate indivisible items to buyers whose values are drawn independently, aiming to maximize consumer surplus after subtracting burnt payments. The authors propose artificial-currency mechanisms, giving each buyer a personalized budget of currency that has no value outside the mechanism. The better of separate selling and these mechanisms achieves a 3-approximation to optimal consumer surplus, holding at every Bayes–Nash equilibrium without equilibrium selection. Both branches are shown to be necessary, since either one alone may capture only a vanishing share of the optimum.

entry.title: L^1 stability of the entropy power inequality in R^d without moment assumptions
entry.summary: L¹ stability of the entropy power inequality in ℝ^d without moment assumptions arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies the stability of Shannon's entropy power inequality in R^d without imposing any moment conditions, giving qualitative results in L^1 and Ruzsa distance. The proof combines Rioul's (2017) optimal transport argument, majorization bounds for density rearrangements, and Christ's (2019) stability result for the sharp form of Young's inequality. The authors also extend recent one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity, continuity of differential entropy, and the equality case of the entropy power inequality to random vectors of any dimension. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report qualitative L1 and Ruzsa-distance stability of the entropy power inequality in R^d without moment assumptions, extending one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity and entropy

entry.title: A paper proving that finding Tarski fixed points in polynomial time is impossible unless certain cryptographic assumptions fail
entry.summary: No Polynomial-Time Algorithm For Tarski Fixed Points Unless Cryptographic Assumptions Fail arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper studies how much computation time is needed to find a Tarski fixed point. The authors give a subexponential-time reduction from the UEOPL problem to finding a Tarski fixed point. Using known cryptographic lower bounds for UEOPL, this yields conditional lower bounds on the running time of any such algorithm, the strongest being quasi-polynomial. These match earlier quasi-polynomial query lower bounds for the problem. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a subexponential reduction from UEOPL to Tarski fixed points, yielding quasi-polynomial conditional lower bounds matching known query bounds.

entry.title: Proof that recognizing k-inducible digraphs is NP-complete
entry.summary: Recognizing k-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies whether a directed graph can be realized as the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. The authors prove that, for every fixed k of at least 3, deciding k-inducibility is NP-complete, settling a long-standing open problem. They also show that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve a long-standing open problem, proving NP-completeness of recognizing k-inducible digraphs for every fixed k≥3, with implications for forbidden-subdigraph characterizations.

entry.title: Deterministic faster algorithm for kidney exchange matching (finding the best set of paired transplants)
entry.summary: Kidney Exchange in Deterministic O^*(4^t+o(t)) Time arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies the kidney exchange problem, which asks for a set of transplants among donor-patient pairs. A randomized algorithm solves it in O*(4^t) time, while the best previous deterministic method needs O*(6.855^t). The authors give a deterministic O*(4^(t+o(t))) algorithm that nearly closes this gap. The framework also handles maximizing additive arc utility among packings with a fixed number of transplants. ★★★★ Notable: Uses dynamic representative sets to reach deterministic 4^{t+o(t)} time, nearly matching the randomized bound, plus extensions to cycles and additive optimization.

entry.title: Computational Complexity of Fair and Stable Data Exchange
entry.summary: The Complexity of Fair and Stable Data Exchange arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies how multiple participants can exchange data fairly and stably, so that each receives returns matching its contribution and no group can profit more by exchanging among itself. The authors show that with submodular utilities, which reflect diminishing returns from overlapping data, approximately reciprocal and core-stable exchanges can be computed efficiently under Shapley sharing. With supermodular utilities, which reflect complementarities, finding approximately reciprocal and core-stable exchanges is PPAD-hard even when contribution credits are easy to evaluate. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate computational complexity of fair, core-stable data exchange: polynomial algorithm for submodular utilities, PPAD-hardness for lattice-supermodular utilities.

entry.title: Weave: Runtime Warp Scheduling for MoE Megakernels That Adapts to Routing
entry.summary: Weave: Routing-Adaptive Runtime Warp Scheduling for MoE Megakernels arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper presents Weave, a megakernel for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers that adjusts how GPU resources are split between communication and computation at runtime, based on routing results. It allocates resources at both SM and warp granularity, and switches warp roles during execution to reduce idle time. The authors report speedups over the strongest baselines, such as 1.30x geomean over DeepGEMM-MegaMoE under EP8 (up to 1.97x on SM103).

entry.title: Code length and optimal power allocation in correlated fading blocks
entry.summary: Coding Length and Optimal Power Allocation in Correlated Block Fading arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies codewords spanning a fixed number of correlated Gaussian fading blocks, where the receiver knows the channel gains and the transmitter knows only their distribution. At fixed average signal-to-noise ratio, decoding error probability must decay exponentially with the number of receive antennas. The authors examine when outage probability predicts the achievable rate and identify a critical block-length-to-array-size ratio above which positive rates are possible. Under a total energy constraint per codeword, they determine the exact limiting rate over all codes for sufficiently large ratios.

entry.title: Asynchronous Byzantine lattice agreement with fast, fault-tolerant consensus on comparable values
entry.summary: Asynchronous Byzantine Lattice Agreement with Logarithmic Response Time and Optimal Resilience arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper presents an asynchronous algorithm for lattice agreement, where processes decide on comparable rather than identical values, under Byzantine failures. It tolerates up to f faulty processes among more than 3f total, requires no authentication, and completes in O(log f) time. The approach extends the classifier-tree framework of Attiya and Rachman and introduces Supported Reliable Broadcast, which combines reliable broadcast with checks that messages are consistent with the sender's prior state.

entry.title: IsoMoE: Placement-Invariant Hybrid CPU-GPU MoE Inference with Lossless 12-bit Experts
entry.summary: IsoMoE: Placement-Invariant Hybrid CPU-GPU MoE Inference with Lossless 12-bit Experts arXiv · Nov 20, 2026IsoMoE is an inference system for Mixture-of-Experts models that splits experts between CPU and GPU while guaranteeing outputs do not change with expert placement. It combines a GPU expert kernel that bitwise replays the CPU kernel's arithmetic, a memory layout enabling efficient lossless 12-bit experts on the CPU using AVX-512, and a dual micro-batch pipeline overlapping CPU and GPU work. Experiments on three MoE models show bitwise identical outputs across placements and an average decoding speedup of 1.26 times, with a maximum of 1.54 times, over the fastest baseline.

entry.title: Balanced Boolean functions from sparse Niho-type permutation polynomials and their few-valued Walsh spectra
entry.summary: Balanced Boolean Functions from Sparse Niho-Type Permutation Polynomials: Few-Valued Walsh Spectra and Applications arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper studies balanced Boolean functions defined through two-to-one mappings P(x+x²) and P(x+x⁻¹), where P is a sparse permutation polynomial of generalized Niho type. For even m it determines the full four-valued Walsh distribution of a function built from Q(x+x²), and it generalizes a permutation polynomial of Gupta and Sharma to a parameterized family over F_{q²}. For each admissible parameter, the complete Walsh distribution is shown to be independent of the parameter. The supports of these functions are also linked to binary codes, hyperplane intersection sets and Cayley graphs.

entry.title: Dual-agent reinforcement learning for joint beamforming and trajectory design in UAV integrated sensing and communication networks
entry.summary: Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies a low-altitude UAV network in which ground base stations provide integrated sensing and communication services to communication UAVs and sensing UAVs. It jointly optimizes ISAC beamforming and UAV trajectories to maximize the average sum rate of communication UAVs, under power, sensing SINR, mission, and collision avoidance constraints. The authors propose DeepDA-OPT, a dual-agent multi-agent deep reinforcement learning scheme trained with the TD3 algorithm. Numerical results indicate higher communication sum rates than baselines, with sensing constraints empirically satisfied and no collisions observed in the evaluated settings.

entry.title: A geometric approach to classifying locally-APN Niho-type power functions
entry.summary: A Geometric Approach to the Classification of Locally-APN Niho-Type Power Functions arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies locally-APN Niho-type power functions over F_{q^2} with q=2^m, using a geometric method. It shows that for F_q-homogeneous functions, the differential conditions hold exactly when the projective graph is a (q+1)-arc in PG(3,q). Using the classification of (q+1)-arcs, the authors characterize when x^{s(q-1)+1} is locally-APN for m≥3, completing the classification and confirming a conjecture by Cui, Luo, and Xiang.

entry.title: Improved Spanning Tree Construction in the HYBRID Model
entry.summary: Improved (Minimum) Spanning Tree Construction in the HYBRID Model arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies spanning tree construction in the HYBRID model, where vertices exchange messages over input edges (local communication) and directly with vertices whose IDs they know (global communication). The authors present a randomized algorithm that, under standard capacity, builds a spanning tree and a well-formed tree in every connected component in O(log n) rounds with high probability. The approach uses a Δ-pseudo-spanning representation, with the main contribution being an O(1)-PSR constructed in O(log n) rounds. The authors also apply this to minimum spanning trees and to computing biconnected components, articulation points, and bridges. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a Δ-pseudo-spanning representation and build an O(1)-PSR in O(log n) rounds under standard capacity, with applications to MST and biconnected components.

entry.title: AceVLN: Asynchronous Cloud-Edge Deployment of Vision-Language Navigation via Latent Scheduling and Compensation
entry.summary: AceVLN: Asynchronous Cloud Edge Deployment of VLNs via Latent Scheduling and Compensation arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper addresses vision-language navigation (VLN) on resource-constrained robots using cloud-edge deployment, where inference and communication delays cause mismatches in latent representations and navigation errors. The authors propose AceVLN, a training-free framework that actively refreshes latent states and compensates on the edge side, guided by feature drift measures in a critical subspace. Experiments report success-rate gains of 1.7 to 2.4 percentage points over the strongest baselines, with 2.7% to 10.0% lower amortized computation time and 18.4% to 22.3% fewer FLOPs.

entry.title: Sequences ensuring each user transmits successfully in multi-packet reception channels
entry.summary: User-Irrepressible Sequences for Multiple-Packet Reception arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies deterministic transmission schemes for slot-synchronous multiple-packet reception channels that use periodic binary protocol sequences, with no feedback or phase synchronization. A sequence set is called γ-UI if every user is guaranteed at least one successful transmission per period, regardless of cyclic shifts. The authors propose a unified explicit construction based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem for any MPR capability γ≥2, and establish the γ-UI property through bounds on pairwise Hamming cross-correlations.

entry.title: Simulating Hard Drive Failure and Lifetime Using Backblaze Data, 2013–2026
entry.summary: Drive Failure and Lifetime Simulation in the Backblaze Drive Statistics Corpus, 2013-2026 arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper tests the assumptions storage simulators make about hard drive lifetimes and failure dependence, using Backblaze's daily records from 2013 to 2026. It compares failure-count forecasts and survival models, examining the effects of drive-model differences, SMART warnings, and shared yearly risks. The authors also provide samplers that represent drive-model differences, shared risks, and changes in drive condition for storage simulations.

entry.title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: counting arrays and when two summaries add up
entry.summary: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies admixed arrays, pairs of matrices recording local ancestry and alleles in the haplotypes of admixed individuals. Under two families of constraints, the authors count diploid admixed arrays and derive asymptotic formulas, using complex martingale techniques, as the number of individuals and loci grow at a bounded ratio. They also examine whether the two summaries carry information additively, and find that additivity holds only on a set of measure zero.

entry.title: Analysis of multi-client inference techniques for vision-language-action models
entry.summary: Analysis of Multi-Client Inference Techniques for Vision-Language-Action Models arXiv · Nov 20, 2026Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are a new class of machine learning models for general-purpose robot control. This paper characterizes how known multi-client techniques, such as batching and co-execution, affect latency, throughput, power, and hardware utilization when serving VLAs. The findings are intended to inform trade-offs and challenges for future multi-VLA serving systems.

entry.title: Joint SLA Admission and Risk Allocation for Cloud Resource Provisioning
entry.summary: Joint SLA Admission and Risk Allocation for Cloud Resource Provisioning arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper studies how a cloud controller should split allowed shortage risk between CPU and memory under a shared SLA limit when forecast-error histories are short or correlated over time. For each split, the controller uses historical forecast errors to set extra reserved capacity, checks whether the history supports that split, and picks the valid option with the lowest combined shortage and idle cost, otherwise falling back to a calibrated policy. In simulation with a 95% joint SLA target and 192 hours of history, it reduced shortage time slots by 1.04 percentage points on average versus always using fallback, at a 0.0091 increase in normalized cost.

entry.title: Contention-aware flexible execution for speeding up concurrent GPU kernels in ML workloads
entry.summary: Contention-Aware Flexible Execution for Machine Learning Workloads arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper examines why running GPU kernels concurrently in machine learning can slow them down, since they compete for shared cores, caches, and memory bandwidth. The authors characterize these slowdowns on AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs, analyzing both performance and memory behavior across memory-bound and compute-bound, large and small kernels. They then propose CAFEML, which tunes operator overlap timing and resource allocation using simple heuristics. Across inference decode, inference prefill, and training, CAFEML achieves up to 13% end-to-end speedup without rewriting kernels.

entry.title: Incentive-Compatible Mechanisms for Fair Sequential Resource Allocation with Private Demands
entry.summary: Incentive Compatible Mechanisms for Sequential Fair Resource Allocation with Private Demands arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies a strategic version of the online fair allocation problem, in which a planner gives a divisible resource to agents over several stages, while each agent's demand is known only to that agent. Because demand is self-reported and money cannot be transferred, agents may misreport their needs. The authors characterize the structure of incentive-compatible allocation rules and identify conditions under which the optimal mechanism has a simple cap structure. They also develop an approximation method that reduces a discretized dynamic program to a longest-path problem on a directed acyclic graph. Numerical experiments show that ignoring strategic reporting can be considerably more costly than enforcing incentive compatibility.

entry.title: DNN-assisted learning to adjust reflecting mirrors and power in light-based wireless networks
entry.summary: DNN-Assisted Deterministic Policy Learning for Adaptive IRS-NOMA-OWC Networks arXiv · Nov 20, 2026This paper studies an indoor light-based wireless network that uses intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) and non-orthogonal multiple access to serve several mobile users. It jointly optimizes power allocation and IRS mirror orientations to maximize the sum rate while meeting each user's quality-of-service requirements. A two-stage framework is proposed, where a deep neural network first estimates user positions and orientations, and a deterministic policy gradient reinforcement learning algorithm then performs the joint optimization. The reported results show better sum rate and fairness than standard reinforcement learning, conventional methods, and networks without IRS, with faster convergence.

entry.title: One Behavior, Out of Order: Deterministic Execution and Parallel Simulation of ROS 2 Applications
entry.summary: One Behavior, Out of Order: Deterministic Execution and Parallel Simulation of ROS 2 Applications arXiv · Nov 20, 2026The paper addresses nondeterminism in ROS 2 applications, where asynchronous publish-subscribe communication makes behavior vary across runs and machines. It proposes a lightweight scheme in which components read inputs and write outputs at predefined instants, making applications deterministic. It also presents an out-of-order parallel simulation algorithm that runs existing ROS 2 applications unchanged. On industrial use cases, the simulator is up to 2.6 times faster than synchronous parallel simulation and uses far less message memory than asynchronous parallel simulation.
